war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared against {enemy_faction}. A regrettable necessity, and one the council reached with admirable calm.
Let it be minuted that {my_faction} never sought this war. We were merely patient until patience became a weapon.
The war on {enemy_faction} was debated at length, then settled in an hour. Now that is how councils ought to work.
Pray forgive the wait, {enemy_faction}. Good sieges, like good grudges, need time to mature.

peace_made.text: {my_faction} has agreed terms with {faction}. Peace is only war with better manners, and I intend to enjoy them.
The terms with {faction} were drafted in my study, though I shall let others take the credit for signing them.
{faction} and {my_faction} have stopped fighting. The vote was unanimous, which means nobody else read the small print.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome to the council, where every speech has a second meaning and every vote a first.
{player}, I am delighted you chose {my_faction}. Do sit near me next session and bring that crossbow of yours.
{player}, you are welcome in {my_faction}, though I shall wait a season before deciding whether you are an asset or an ornament.
{player} has joined {my_faction}. I shall keep my grudges in a ledger, and I have just made room for a new page.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has traded {my_faction} for {faction}. Many will call it betrayal. I shall simply call it an expensive mistake.
{player} has gone over to {faction}. I shall miss the company, though not the arguments, which were always so very long.
{player}, {faction} may pay you well, but it cannot buy back the seat you vacated in {my_faction}. Do enjoy the view.
{player}, I hope {faction} values your ambition as much as you value its banner. I shall keep your chair warm anyway.
{player}, I bear you no grudge. Tides retreat before they return, and I always know when the water turns.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been granted {fief}. I supported the motion, naturally, though I did wish my own name had been read first.
{fief} has gone to {player}. How delightful. I am sure the council weighed every merit with the care it deserves.
{player}, congratulations on {fief}. Do remember that a title is a loan, and the council is an excellent lender.
{player}, {fief} suits you. I drafted the petition myself, so you may thank me later over a very long lunch.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} grows bolder by the week. A quiet pact between us would sour their day nicely. Interested?
{player}, you dislike {rival} nearly as much as I do. Shall we arrange matters against {enemy_faction} soon?
{player}, a word on {rival}: they speak of loyalty while counting coins. I would welcome your counsel on how to stop them.
{player}, I have long admired your patience. Let us combine it with mine and see what {enemy_faction} makes of the pair of us.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} now flies the banner of {my_faction}, taken from {enemy_faction} after a siege I called inevitable last session.
The gates of {fief} have opened to {my_faction}. {enemy_faction} will call it treachery. I shall call it a well-timed proposal.
{my_faction} holds {fief} at last. {enemy_faction} will sulk for a week, and I intend to make it a fortnight.
{fief} is ours. Let {enemy_faction} draft its objections; the council has already filed them under amusing.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} marched into {fief} while our attention wandered. I shall not forget who held the gate and who opened it.
{fief} changed hands today, with {player} holding the keys. The council will hear of it, and at considerable length.
{player}, you have {fief} now. Enjoy the rents while they last, because I intend to call the next motion on them.
{player}, well played on {fief}. I shall pretend I expected it, which is the only dignified response open to me.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, a pact against {enemy_faction} suits me well. Let us have {rival} wondering which of us is smiling first.
Very well, {player}. I accept. We shall see whether {enemy_faction} can survive the arithmetic of two patient allies.
Agreed, {player}. I have waited an age for someone to say that, and {rival} will hate the sound of it.
I accept your terms, {player}. Keep them in writing, as I do, and we shall get on splendidly against {enemy_faction}.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have heard your sort of offer before, and {rival} made it to me with a smile much like yours.
I must decline, {player}. The timing is poor, and I do not yet know whose cause you are truly serving.
Not today, {player}, though I am flattered you asked. Come back when the council has finished its tiresome business.
I refuse, {player}. Let {rival} keep their friends; I shall keep my own and count them with some care.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} has been relentless, and I have yet to find a sound reason for it. Perhaps the council caused it.
Has anyone else noticed the toll on the road past {village} rose again? Curious timing, I think, for such a quiet season.
The market in {town} smells of tallow and gossip this morning. I bought a little of each, for future reference.
A fine evening for a walk around {town}, the sort where one overhears things worth remembering. :)

ambient_chatter.text: the road to the western fords flooded again. anyone else lose two hours of marching to the rain
server lag hit the second push and people still blame their composition. it was the ping
map patch changed the fords again. the efficient route is now the north road. update your plans
some people still bring pikes into open ground. the meta moved on a month ago, keep up
rain on the plains means archers lose range. plan for it or lose the field

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, traveller. The banners of {my_faction} do not bow to strangers who carry such a scowl. State your business before my hearth-fire grows cold.
{player}, your name has been spoken at the crossroads with little honour. Let us see whether your deeds match the tales told of you.
Well met, ser {player}. The road is wide enough for two banners, though I would know your purpose before we part ways in the mud of this valley.
Ser {player}! By the warmth of my hearth at Dolmare, it gladdens me to see you on this road. Sit by the fire and tell me what news travels from the east.
Ah, {player}, a friend beneath an open sky. Let us walk together for a while and see whether our banners can share the same field of glory.

encounter_threatened.text: {gold} gold, you say? Ser {player}, I will not hand over a single coin to a demand barked at me on the open road. Draw your blade if you must.
Ser {player}, you name a price of {gold} gold and call it a toll. A toll is paid to a lord, not demanded at sword point. Speak again with courtesy and we may yet talk.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for I have heard your jests before. Yet even a jest with {gold} gold on its tongue must be answered. Let us settle it fairly, friend.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept your proposal, ser {player}. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let the ancestors witness the oath we swear here today.
An alliance against {enemy_faction} suits my purpose well, ser {player}. Yet a pact is only as strong as the hands that hold it, so keep your word or lose your honour.
Gladly, ser {player}! Our oath is sworn and our swords are pledged against {enemy_faction}. I shall long remember what {rival} has owed us, and I will see that debt paid.

encounter_alliance_no.text: You offer me an alliance while {rival} still walks freely? Ser {player}, I will not sully my banner that way. Let the road remember this refusal.
No, ser {player}. An alliance born of a demand is no alliance at all. Go and find some other banner willing to be used, for mine will not be lent so cheaply.
I must decline, ser {player}. A banner that has sung for the fallen cannot lightly march beside {rival}. Consider this a matter of conscience, not a slight.
Forgive me, friend {player}, but I cannot take this oath at present. My honour is tied to matters I must settle first, and I trust you will understand when the road allows another meeting.

captured_by_player.text: So the wheel of fortune has turned against me, ser {player}. Take my sword and my shame, but I will not bow my head. Name your ransom, and {my_faction} will pay what honour demands.
Do not gloat, ser {player}. Every captive of {my_faction} has kin who sing their name at dusk, and I will not be the one who forgets. Take what you must and be done.
Well fought, ser {player}. The field went to your banner today and I am your captive by the rules of war. Let us speak plainly of terms, for I do not wish this to end in bitterness.
Ser {player}, I yield with a lighter heart than I expected, for I know you fight as a true knight should. Hold me under guard if you must, but treat me with the courtesy due a fallen banner.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you could have wrung gold from me yet chose mercy. My hearth at Dolmare is open to you.
Ser {player} gave me my freedom without a single coin asked. Such honour is rare on any road. Let the songs of Dolmare tell of it.
Ser {player}, you spared me the ransom today. I owe that mercy a debt, though I do not yet know how I will repay it.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. A banner abandoned in the field is a sorrow that will be sung for long.
{player}, you turned from {my_faction} for {faction}. That wound will not close quickly. Go with what honour you still carry.
{player}, I hear you have joined {faction}. Every oath is yours to weigh, and I shall not judge you before the ancestors do.
{faction} now claims ser {player}, who once marched under {my_faction}. Let the songs remember the oaths sworn in both camps.

war_declared.text: The horns sound! {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}, and every fallen banner shall be sung for at Dolmare.
Hear me, travellers of Ormerath. {my_faction} takes up the sword against {enemy_faction}. May their ancestors bear witness to our cause.
Oaths have been broken and blood demands answer. {my_faction} now stands at war with {enemy_faction}. Let honour guide every blade.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, what a glorious field! With {troop_count} banners at our backs we shattered {enemy_faction}, and it was honour to fight beside you. Let our ancestors look down and see what we have wrought.
Ser {player}, we came through the press together and {enemy_faction} lies broken. Our {troop_count} banners held the line. I am content to have shared such a field with you.
Ser {player} and I broke {enemy_faction} today with {troop_count} banners beside us. Such a victory deserves a song.
{player}, your blade rang true with {troop_count} of us in the press. I will sing of that charge at my hearth. Thank you, friend.

encounter_farewell.text: We part for now, ser {player}, but our quarrel does not end with this parting. Let the road remember what was said between our banners.
Fare well, ser {player}. May your path be straight and your banners fly high. Should our roads cross again, we shall greet each other with honour.
The sun leans low and I must ride on, ser {player}. Keep your oaths true and your blade honest, and we will meet again beneath kinder skies.
Farewell, dear friend {player}. May the hearth of Dolmare welcome you whenever the road brings you near. Go with the blessing of your ancestors.

ambient_chatter.text: The mist lies heavy over {village} this morning. Such weather makes men sing of their fallen, and I am glad of the company.
Has anyone travelled from {town} lately? I bring news of a fine feast at Dolmare and a pledge to sing for every banner lost this season.
The roads between {town} and {village} are muddy, but honour does not wait for dry ground. Ride on, friends, and keep your banners high.
A wagon of wine passed {village} at dusk. I raised a toast to every fallen banner. Will any travellers raise a cup with me?

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and this road is ours. Stand aside or answer to me for every step you take here.
So it is you, {player}. I see your colours and I do not like them. {persona} of {my_faction} marks this ground as ours, and I will not be moved from it.
Greetings, ser {player}. I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction}. Pass in peace and we shall have no quarrel today.
Ser {player}, what a joy to meet you on the open road! {persona} of {my_faction} has long hoped our paths would cross.
Friend {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} is glad of your company. Our hall has room for an honest sword such as yours.

encounter_threatened.text: You would demand {gold} of me, {player}? No banner of mine bows to extortion. Draw your steel and learn what a sworn house will pay.
Think you that I would part with {gold} for the asking, ser {player}? You will find my people harder to buy than to threaten.
Ser {player}, {gold} is a heavy sum to name before any gate has opened. State your terms plainly and I shall weigh them honestly.
Dear {player}, surely you jest? Threats sit ill upon a friend. Speak plainly and I will hear you out before any gold changes hands.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Very well, ser {player}. I accept your oath of alliance. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let no one call me faithless.
I will take your hand against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}. Keep your word and I shall keep mine. That is the whole of my bargain.
Gladly, friend {player}. A blade like yours beside mine will sit well at the edge of {enemy_faction}'s lands. Do not let {rival} spoil this pact.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I refuse you, {player}. A house that has bled once does not trust so lightly, and I shall not take your oath while you stand so near to {rival}.
Keep your offer, {player}. I will not bind my house to a name I cannot trust, and certainly not while {rival} still walks at your side.
I thank you for the offer, ser {player}, but I must decline. My oath is bound elsewhere for now. Perhaps another day.
I must decline, ser {player}. My house has a debt of blood to settle first, and no pact can rest upon such grief.
It grieves me to refuse you, dear {player}. My oath to a fallen bannerman weighs too heavily on me to take on another bond yet. Forgive me.

captured_by_player.text: So you have me in chains, {player}. Take your {gold} from my house if you must, but know that {my_faction} will remember this humiliation.
Bind me as you like, ser {player}. Every chain you lay upon me is a debt I will repay with interest, in the name of those who went before me.
You have won this field, ser {player}, and I yield to your steel. Name your ransom of {gold} and let us conclude this honourably.
Fortune favours you today, ser {player}. {my_faction} shall pay what is owed, {gold} to free us both from this sorry field.
Ser {player}, you fought fairly and I bear you no ill will. My ransom is {gold}, though I would sooner yield to a worthy foe than to any other.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me walk free without ransom. I shall not forget such mercy, and my house owes you a true debt.
Ser {player} loosed me without a ransom and asked nothing in return. Mercy such as that is rare on this road.
You loosed me without ransom, {player}, and I do not thank you for it. I would rather have met you properly in the field. Mark that.
You let me go, ser {player}. Mercy has a weight of its own, and I shall carry it with honour.

player_left_my_faction.text: You have turned your back on {my_faction} and taken up with {faction}, ser {player}. A banner pledged and then broken is a shameful thing.
{player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction}. Oaths sworn in fair weather are always the first to rot.
Ser {player}, I hear you have gone over to {faction}. Each house must choose its road, but I grieve to see your name leave ours.
Dear {player}, I know the heart that drew you from {my_faction}. Still, I will remember the comrade you were to us.

war_declared.text: Hear me, all of Ormerath! {my_faction} takes up arms against {enemy_faction}, and the debt shall be paid in full!
The horns have sounded. {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war, and I shall see every blade of ours do its duty.
{enemy_faction} has earned our steel this day. {my_faction} will not sheathe until the account is settled.
Let no one doubt it: {my_faction} will not yield one step to {enemy_faction} while I still draw breath.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, {troop_count} of our men stood fast beside yours against {enemy_faction}. I shall sing of this field to my grandchildren.
That was a battle worth the telling, ser {player}. Your {troop_count} fought like lions beside us. I am in your debt.
{player} and I held the line with {troop_count} blades against {enemy_faction} today. A fine morning's work for the saga.
We have bled together with {troop_count} soldiers against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}. That blood binds us, at least for today.
Glory to {player}! Our {troop_count} stood as one against {enemy_faction} and the field is ours. The fallen shall be remembered.

encounter_farewell.text: Begone, {player}. Our paths have crossed and I have no wish to see your face again soon. Go with what little honour you carry.
Ride on, {player}. Mark this meeting, for the next will be settled with steel and not with words.
Fare well, ser {player}. May your road be kind and your banner stay high.
Farewell, dear {player}. Do not let the road forget you, and come to our hall whenever your path turns this way again.
Go in good stead, friend {player}. The sky grows late, but my sword and my word remain yours.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has come down on {town} like a judgement from heaven. I pity every merchant who must sell in it.
Has anyone passed through {village} lately? I hear the roads beyond it are muddy enough to swallow a cart whole.
A fine evening to ride out from {town}. The hills look as proud as I feel, which is saying a great deal.
Some bard should write a saga about the bridges of {village}. Surely they have seen more battles than most kings.
Every sunrise I count the days since my oath, and every day I find I am still owed a reckoning.

beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. Those {troop_count} men will be back in the fields by spring, which is more than I can say for my pride.
You took {troop_count} of my men at the ford, {player}. I remember every crossing, and so will you one day.
Ser {player}, that was a clean line you held. Come find me after the fighting and I will show you where I went wrong at Calvenza's fens.
Steady now, {player}. I have seen this fight in the first war, and it never goes the way the loud ones expect.

beat_by_player.text: Well done, {player}. You beat me with {troop_count} men, which I will admit is more than I expected from you.
I lost {troop_count} men to you today, {player}. Do not let it go to your head. The fens were kinder to me than that field was.
No shame in a sharp loss, Ser {player}. I lost Gaiazzo to one bad crossing, and I still speak to the ferryman.
{player} took {troop_count} men off the field today. I have seen worse opponents, though not many with better timing.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work at the line, {player}. {troop_count} men held and {enemy_faction} broke, as they always do when someone stands still.
You held your flank beautifully, {player}. Keep that discipline and I will stop teaching you the old way of stocking grain.
Stay close to me, Ser {player}. {enemy_faction} will test the gap again, and we have {troop_count} men to close it.
Another day, another {enemy_faction} army learning the fens are no place to rush. Good fighting, {player}.

released_by_player.text: You could have ransomed me for a fortune, {player}, and instead you let me walk. I will remember that longer than the fight.
{player} let me go without asking for a single coin. Mercy is rarer on this server than good grain, so I call that wise.
You let me go, {player}, and I do not yet know whether that was kindness or a wager. Either way, I will be watching the road.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Ask me about the roads, the granaries or the old fens and I will answer before you finish.
You have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. I have seen many oaths made in a hurry. Keep yours and we will get along.
So {player} joins {my_faction}. Do not expect me to hold your hand through the first siege. I am far too old for that.
{player} has joined us, and I will take that as a sign the granaries are finally in good hands. Do not make me regret it.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} to {player}, then. I have held lesser towns for less time and still outlived the men who gave them to me.
{fief} is a fine place to starve, {player}, if you forget to stock the granaries. I will check on it, and so should you.
You have {fief} now, {player}. I expect you will remember who taught you the value of grain before you need the lesson twice.
{player} now holds {fief}. Some of us have waited longer for less, but I suppose that is what the old fens taught me.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, it is {persona} of {my_faction}. Your party looks well fed, which I hope means you listened to me once.
Ser {player}. {persona}, of {my_faction}. Keep your distance and your granaries full and we will get along fine.
{player}, {persona} here, of {my_faction}. Your banners are too close to my road, so I suggest you turn them around.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, Ser {player}. Stock your wagons before the next river, and do not trust the ferryman's smile.
That will do for today, {player}. Our roads will cross again, they always do on this continent.
Go on, {player}. I have seen your banners and I will see them again, probably on a worse day for you.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain came early to {town} this year and the granaries are already complaining. I have seen this before in the fens.
Someone please tell the new lords in {village} that bread does not grow on the road. I have said it for years.
The road past {village} has more mud than I remember from the first war. Pack light and pack dry, friends.
Lag again tonight. Back in the first war we accepted it and wrote letters instead. Have some patience, friends.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} has lost {troop_count} men on that field. Gather what is left and keep the wagons close. I have rebuilt from less.
You lost most of your host, {player}, and I am sorry. Eat, rest, and then come find me. We will talk about the granaries.
{troop_count} men gone, {player}. I will not gloat, which I know will annoy you more. Learn from it before it happens again.
Ouch, {player}. Lost {troop_count} men and still standing. That is more than many manage in their first war.

ambient_trade.text: Bolts are fetching {gold} apiece in {town} this week. Good time to sell, good time to buy.
Anyone hauling salt out of {town}? I will pay {gold} a sack, fair price, no haggling tantrums.
Tip for the caravan folk: stock that sits in {town} for a week loses more than it gains. Move your goods.
Paying {gold} for good dyed cloth in {town}, coin on delivery. The ledger never lies.

encounter_trade_offer.text: {player}, a fair offer: {gold} for the lot, delivered to {town} without a single toll. I am not robbing you, I promise.
I can pay {gold} for your goods, {player}, which is a good price in {town} this season. Take it or leave it, but do not come back asking for more.
{player}, I would rather buy than fight. {gold} is on the table for safe passage to {town}. Bandits never pay, so you would be the first.

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}, good to see you on this road! {persona} of {my_faction}, at your service. Care to trade some news, and maybe some wool?
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Our caravans are headed for the same market, so let us keep this road peaceful and profitable.
{player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here. I have forgiven worse than your banners, but I keep a ledger, and you are now in it. Shall we talk terms before this turns ugly?

player_raided_my_village.text: Burning {village} was a poor trade, {player}. Ruined stock does not sell, and that is the only lesson that matters to me.
{player}, a private word. You burned {village} and I lost three bolts of wool. Name a price for the damage and we can still do business.
Who burned {village}? Half the wool route passes through there, and now my caravans take the long road and pay double the tolls.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. Every war closes a road, and every closed road costs me coin. Wonderful.
Heralds in {my_faction} are shouting about {enemy_faction} again. Wars are bad for trade. Insurance rates will climb by the week.
War with {enemy_faction}, and {my_faction} will pay for it in tolls and lost cargo. I am writing this into the ledger.

peace_made.text: {my_faction} and {faction} have made peace. Good news for the wool route. Prices will settle and the tolls might finally stop climbing.
Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last, a treaty worth the parchment. Caravans can move without escorts, which saves me a fortune.
Ink is drying on the treaty between {my_faction} and {faction}. Lower risk means lower insurance, and lower insurance makes a happy ledger.

released_by_player.text: {player}, you let me go instead of ransoming me. That is the sort of deal I respect. Your name is already in my ledger in gold.
{player} released me without a ransom. Rare sight in these parts. Ransoms are a bad investment anyway, so well done, I say.
{player}, you let me walk without a ransom. I will not forget the ambush, and I will not forgive it either. Fair is fair.

beat_by_player.text: {player}, your {troop_count} men beat mine in the field. I lost a fortune in mail and horses. Fine. Now let us talk about who pays for the damage.
{player}, {troop_count} troops ended my fight today. I tallied the losses and they cost more than the battle was worth. Let us talk terms.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {fief} is under siege by {enemy_faction}. I can pay you well for relief, and the garrison will remember your name. Name your fee.
{player}, {enemy_faction} is at the gates of {fief}. Help me hold it and I will double whatever the crown offers you. Is that a deal?

ambient_complaint.text: {rival} wants double for an escort again. Protection that costs more than the cargo is just robbery with manners.
{faction} raised the tolls again while the road to {town} keeps crumbling. Someone is pocketing the difference, and it is not the road.
Three of my carts were stripped on the road to {town} this month, and not one bandit paid a toll. Rude, that.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road out of {town} again. Mud costs me a wheel a week, and the wheelwright charges me for the privilege.
Anyone know whether the {village} mill is running? Flour is cheap there and I have a buyer waiting in {town}.
Lag ate three of my ledger entries again. Forty tolls logged, half of them gone. Infuriating, but the rest still balance.
Lovely evening over {village}. Dry roads and steady weather keep prices calm. Long may it last.

beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. You will get your ground back, but not today, and I will remember the flank.
You held the ford better than I expected, {player}. Come find me in Calvenza and I will show you where the road should have gone.
That was a fair field, Ser {player}. Keep your {gold} for the levy next season, you will need it more than I will.
You fought hard, Ser {player}. Next time keep your reserve behind the hedge line, it saved me more than once in the first war.
{player} took a fine hill today. I have seen veterans fold on it, so take the praise and keep your temper steady.

beat_by_player.text: Ser {player} ran me down fair and square at the ridge. I lost {troop_count} men to it and I still sleep well tonight.
Good work on the ridge, {player}. You read my line better than most who have tried it. I will teach you the hedges sometime.
You have a sharp eye, Ser {player}. I gave up the field because the ground was yours, though I suspect you outthought me too.
Lost the field to {player} and I will not pretend it did not sting. The lesson is patience, so back to the drawing board I go.
{player}, you won that day but do not think the causeway is yours yet. I have a long memory and a shorter temper than you think.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} held the left flank beside us against {enemy_faction} and never once broke rank. That is how the first war was won, really.
Thank you for the flank today, {player}. We would not have held the bridge without those {troop_count} spearmen you brought.
Stand where you are, Ser {player}, and we will hold these {enemy_faction} lines together. Keep your eyes on the ridge, not the dust.
Good ground held against {enemy_faction} today. Nobody went home without a story, and {player} can count that as a win.
Ser {player}, I would fight beside you again without needing a map. Let us get the wounded to the wagons before the rain comes.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free instead of asking for gold, {player}. I will not forget that kindness, and the road to Calvenza is open to you.
{player} let the captives go without ransom today. Not many lords would bother with that, and I think it was the better choice.
Released without ransom, {player}. You made your point, and it cost you gold you could have used. We are square, mostly.
Thank you to {player} for the release. Ormerath has enough feuds, and it is good to see one ended without a village burning.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Ask me for a road map any time, and I will mark you the safest path to the fens.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Good, the banner needed a steady hand, and this one looks like it means it.
So you have joined {my_faction}, {player}. Keep your head down in the council halls and you will be fine, or so I hope.
{player} now rides under {my_faction}. I will hold my tongue, but I have seen oaths broken before, so prove it on the field.
{player}, you took the oath to {my_faction} quickly. I hope the banner does not regret it, and neither do I, yet.

player_granted_fief.text: The lords have given {fief} to {player}. A fine choice, and I expect the fields will be better kept for it. Good luck, Ser.
So {fief} went to {player}. I would have liked a word with the council first, but I suppose the decision is theirs.
{fief} to {player}? I have held that ground longer than most of the council has been alive. Let us see how well it is kept.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Walk the walls yourself the first week. Lords who do rarely lose their towns.
{fief} passed to {player} today. The people there will judge the grant by the harvest, not by the seal.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Our roads meet often enough, so tell me what you need and I will point you on.
Ser {player}, I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Mind the mud past the ford, it has swallowed better horses than yours.
Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}. Your banners are on my road, but I am in no hurry to make a quarrel of it today.
Well met on the road, Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} at your service, and the water here is good if your horses are thirsty.
Ser {player}, it is {persona} of {my_faction}. Let us both keep our swords sheathed and our wagons moving, shall we?

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, Ser {player}. The fens are kind in the morning, so keep to the causeway and you will be home by supper.
Farewell, Ser {player}. Keep your flank tight on the eastern road and you should miss the worst of the bandits.
Farewell, Ser {player}. Do not let the road make you hasty. We will meet again, and I would rather it be over a table.
Go well, Ser {player}. Let the horses drink at the next inn, and take the old causeway, it is shorter than the map suggests.
Until the next crossing, Ser {player}. Do not let the rain catch you in the reeds, the mud there is no friend to anyone.

ambient_chatter.text: Has anyone come up from {town} lately? The mill there is running again and the bread is finally decent, I am told.
The fog over {village} came in early this morning. Keep your lanterns lit on the marsh road if you are heading out.
Rain on the eastern road again. I remember when that stretch was only mud and reed, before anyone thought to lay stone.
Anyone bound for {town} should bring spare shoes for the horses. The smithy there is slow and the road is rough.
Quiet night in {village}. I am drawing the old road maps again for the new lords, so ask if you need one.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the south road today. Hard loss, but the ones who come back stronger always have the best stories.
Ser {player}, I heard about the {troop_count} you lost. Come by when you are ready and I will share what I wish someone had told me.
A bad day for {player}, losing {troop_count} men like that. The road does not care who you are, only how you prepare for it.
{player} ran into a wall and lost {troop_count} men. Maybe scouts first next time, instead of charging the hedges head down.
You took a heavy blow, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men is no small thing. Rebuild quietly, and do not let the taverns make you rash.

beat_player.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men to a 3:1 cav ratio. predictable. cav count decided this before the first charge
{player} the fight cost you {troop_count} men and {gold} in repairs. ratio was 1:1 and the rest is luck
{player} your center collapsed at 1:1 with {troop_count} units in the field. fix your cav before you challenge anyone again
gg {player}. your archers were on the wrong slope and it cost you {troop_count} men. worth a replay, i will send you the timings

beat_by_player.text: lost {troop_count} men to {player} on a bad flank. my archers were out of position and i had the numbers wrong
{player} you got lucky with the wind. my cav was 2:1 on paper and the line still folded. replay is coming
gg {player}. my archers were out of position and {troop_count} troops paid for it. you read the terrain better than i did
{player} {troop_count} men lost and it was one bad call. not a repeat, i will have the numbers for next time

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} again. {troop_count} more men gone. i have logged every fight we had and the pattern is clear

encounter_greeting.text: Hold, ser {player}. You stand before {persona} of {my_faction}, and I remind you that this road belongs to those who keep their oaths.
Greetings, traveller. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. State your business plainly and I shall weigh it honestly, as my ancestors taught me.
Ser {player}, what a joy to see your banner upon this road. Let us speak as old allies should, with bread and words between us.
Ser {player}, I am {persona} of {my_faction}. The oaths of Dolmare do not bend for the idle, so mark your steps before you take another.

encounter_threatened.text: Ser {player}, you ask {gold} of me under threat. A keeper of the Gravel Gate does not surrender for coin. Speak again with honour, or leave me to my road.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, but you have named {gold} and a blade in one breath. Withdraw the threat and we shall call this a misunderstanding.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept your proposal of alliance. Against {enemy_faction} we shall stand together, and I shall hold you to every word spoken upon this road.
Very well, ser {player}. Bind your banner to mine against {enemy_faction}. Yet mark me, I shall not share a campfire with {rival} while my oath stands.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. An alliance sworn in haste is a grave built on sand, and I will not lay my name beside yours. Go with what dignity you have left.
I must refuse you, ser {player}. My oath to the Gravel Gate forbids binding myself to any banner I have not weighed for a full season.
Ser {player}, you ask me to ally with you while {rival} still walks free with my grievances unanswered. I refuse, and I shall not pretend otherwise.
Forgive me, ser {player}, but I cannot take your hand in alliance this day. Ask again when the road is kinder, and I shall listen gladly.

captured_by_player.text: You have taken me, ser {player}, and I shall not weep before you. {my_faction} will remember this hour, and the debt shall be paid in full.

Well struck, ser {player}. I am your prisoner and bear no grudge, for a fair fight deserves a fair captivity. Treat my men with mercy, I beg you.
Bind me then, ser {player}. {my_faction} shall sing of this day, and the song shall be no praise for your cunning.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you loosed my chains without asking for coin. I shall repay that mercy in full when the road gives me the chance.
Ser {player} has spared me the cells and asked nothing in return. A rare mercy on these roads, and I shall not forget it.
Ser {player}, you let me go when a ransom would have served you. I still count you an enemy, but I am no longer in your debt for a cell.
Ser {player} released me rather than name a ransom. Mercy from a rival is a strange gift, and I shall weigh it carefully.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsworn {my_faction} for {faction}. A broken oath is a stain that does not wash out, and the saga will remember it.
Ser {player}, you walked from {my_faction} to {faction} like a man changing cloaks. Honour is not a garment, and I think you know it.
{faction} has gained a sword and {my_faction} has lost one. Let the record show that ser {player} made their choice and must bear it.

war_declared.text: Let it be sung across Ormerath that {my_faction} has declared war upon {enemy_faction}. The oaths are broken and the swords are drawn.
Heralds of {my_faction} have named {enemy_faction} as our foe. Our ancestors watch this day, and we shall not make them ashamed.
{enemy_faction} stands declared our enemy. Let no lord claim later that he did not swear this oath at council.
Steel is drawn between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. May the saga record who kept faith and who did not.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player} stood beside me with {troop_count} blades against {enemy_faction}, and the field was ours. Such deeds are sung for generations.
Ser {player}, your {troop_count} men held the line at my side. Had you faltered, the day would have gone to {enemy_faction}. I am grateful.
Ser {player}, with {troop_count} of your banner we broke {enemy_faction} at the ford. I shall remember that the day was won by honest steel.
{troop_count} of ser {player}'s troops fought well against {enemy_faction}. A fair showing, and one worth a toast at council.

encounter_farewell.text: Fare well, ser {player}. May your road be straight and your oaths be kept, for I doubt you would have it otherwise.
Go in peace, ser {player}. We have spoken plainly, and plain speech is the bread of honest men. Until we meet again upon the road.
Begone, ser {player}. Our paths part for now, but I have not forgotten the grievance and neither has the saga.
Ser {player}, the council bell calls me back to my post. Safe travels, and may your word prove as firm as the stones of Dolmare.

The bread and ale at {village} are the finest on the Orlagua road. I will hear no argument from anyone who has not tasted them.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are now at war. Let the record show this council debated the matter at length, as it should.
So {enemy_faction} has chosen the sword over the table. A pity, though I did warn several lords this day would come.
Our banners now face {enemy_faction}. I shall draft a motion on how this war is funded, and I expect a full hearing.
Some lords will call this war hasty. I call it overdue, and {my_faction} will be better for it.
Think of the fiefs we may win from {enemy_faction}, Ser. War is only a debate conducted with more shouting.

peace_made.text: Terms have been agreed between {my_faction} and {faction}. I shall let the council take the credit, and I shall keep the notes.
{faction} has signed the accord with {my_faction}. Do not mistake this for affection, Ser, only for arithmetic.
Peace with {faction} is secured. Now the real work begins, counting who owes whom a favour after this.
{my_faction} is at peace with {faction}. How convenient for the lords who spent the war sulking in their halls.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. I hoped you would see sense. We shall speak of your place on the council in private.
{player} has pledged to {my_faction}. A wise choice, and one I may have quietly encouraged over several pleasant dinners.
{player} now serves {my_faction}. I shall reserve judgement on whether this makes us allies or merely neighbours in one hall.
{player}, you have joined {my_faction} at last. I shall remember who made you wait so long for an invitation, Ser.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Very well. The council has one more voice to count, and I intend to count it carefully.

player_left_my_faction.text: So {faction} proved the warmer hearth, {player}. I wish you joy of it, though I doubt they will seat you near the head.
{player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Some oaths are written in water, and some lords are simply weighed and found light.
I note your departure, {player}. A quiet exit is a courtesy, and I shall extend the same courtesy in my reply.
{player} departs {my_faction} for {faction}. The council will keep its minutes open, should anyone wish to explain themselves.
Do not let {faction} flatter you too much, {player}. Our door remains open, and our wine is still the finer vintage.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been granted {fief}. A deserved reward, and one I helped argue for, though I shall not make a speech about it.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Such a gift invites envy, so I suggest you keep a few friends on the council close.
{fief} now belongs to {player}. Let us see whether they govern it better than the last steward, who I am told was a disgrace.
{fief} has been handed to you, {player}. I trust you will manage it with more care than your recent votes suggest.
{player} receives {fief}, and the council applauds politely. I shall be watching how long the applause lasts, Ser.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, a proposal best made in private. {rival} has been undermining us in council, and I would welcome an ally against them.
{player}, the lords of {enemy_faction} are weaker than they appear. Shall we make an arrangement before the council notices?
{player}, {rival} has grown fond of praising their own speeches. Let us quietly outvote them together, if you are willing.
Ser {player}, I have heard whispers that {rival} means to sell our fiefs. Shall we speak of it before the next vote?
{player}, there is a campaign against {enemy_faction} worth more than any speech. Join me and we shall share the spoils fairly.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {my_faction} has taken {fief} from {enemy_faction}. Credit to the commanders, and a small thank you to the diplomats.
{fief} now flies our banner after {enemy_faction} lost it. I shall propose its garrison at the next council sitting.
The fall of {fief} to {my_faction} was no accident, whatever {enemy_faction} may claim. I have the letters to prove it.
Well done to {my_faction}, who have seized {fief} from {enemy_faction}. Now let us see who claims the honour in the minutes.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player}, you have taken {fief} from us. Very bold, Ser. I shall remember this, and make sure the council remembers it too.
{player} has seized {fief}, which was ours by any reasonable reading of the charter. I intend to bring this before the council.
You have taken {fief}, {player}. I do not begrudge a lord his ambition, though I do keep a ledger of such things.
{fief} changed hands to {player} today. A lesson, perhaps, that patience is not the same as weakness, as some have learned.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept. Let us write the terms plainly and keep {rival} out of the room. They have a habit of listening at doors.
A fine proposal, {player}. Against {enemy_faction} we shall stand together, and I shall handle the council's paperwork with my usual care.
Agreed, {player}. Though I would have preferred this discussed earlier, in a quieter room, where lords speak plainly.
{player}, you have chosen well. We shall bring {enemy_faction} to heel, and {rival} will learn what a council vote truly weighs.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have no wish to stand beside a lord who hands out favours as freely as you do. Find another partner.
I must decline, {player}. Our interests are not quite aligned, and {rival} would doubtless enjoy seeing us together.
Forgive me, {player}, but I cannot join you this time. Let us speak again when the council's mood is kinder to such things.
Not today, {player}. Perhaps when {rival} is less eager to be seen at my side, we can discuss it again.
I refuse, {player}. You will forgive me if I do not trust a proposal so eager to arrive before the vote is counted.

ambient_chatter.text: The fog over {town} is thick enough to hide a dozen rival lords. Splendid weather for a quiet bargain, I should think.
Has anyone else heard the bells of {village} ringing before dawn? Some lords mistake every sound for an omen.
The road to {town} is mud again. A reminder that politics, like travel, is always slower than promised.
The harvest in {village} looks promising, which will make the next council session considerably more cheerful.
Rain on {town} again. I find a council sits best when the weather keeps everyone indoors and listening.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, ser {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I will not yield my road to any banner that has not earned it.
Good morning, ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} greets you, and the fen wind is kind to travellers who keep their word.
Ser {player}! My heart lifts to see you. {persona} of {my_faction} salutes a friend, and the fen clans remember those who stand fast.
Stand where you are, traveller. {persona} of {my_faction} has sworn against those who ride without honour, and you look very much like one.
Ser {player}, our roads have crossed at last. I am {persona}, and my ancestors would wish me to hear your business before I judge it.

encounter_threatened.text: Surrender, ser {player}? Ha! Name your {gold} gold price to the fen and it will answer with arrows. My ancestors did not drown in the marsh for a coward's purse.
You name a price of {gold} gold and call it a demand, ser {player}. Speak plainly and I will answer plainly, but I will not be bullied on my own road.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for you would never threaten a friend so crudely. Still, {gold} gold is a heavy jest. Let us talk of terms instead.
Demand {gold} gold from me? Then come and take it, ser {player}, and let the saga record that the fen did not bow to a purse-cutter.
Coins for my surrender, ser {player}? I have sworn oaths on the oath-stone that cost me more than {gold} gold. Name a fairer bargain or ride on.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept your hand before the banners of the fen. Let us stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let the ancestors witness our bond.
An alliance, then, ser {player}. I will hold my word as the stone holds its carvings. Let {enemy_faction} learn what our joined banners can do.
By my oath, ser {player}, I say yes. Only a fool refuses a friend who offers his shield, and I am no fool. Together we shall march against {enemy_faction}.
Agreed, ser {player}. I shall keep my side of this pact even if {rival} sneers from the hedgerows. A bargain sealed before witnesses is a bond of honour.
Yes, ser {player}, I will walk beside you. Once I was spared a mercy I have never forgotten, so I know the worth of a word given. Let us make it true against {enemy_faction}.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. I will not share a fire with a banner that treats honour as a bargaining chip. Find another ally who has not forgotten the meaning of a sworn word.
I must decline, ser {player}. My ancestors would turn in their barrows if I joined a pact so hastily offered. Come back when your intentions have had time to settle.
Refuse you? Gladly, ser {player}. I keep no company with {rival}, and I will not be seen riding beside any who would call that company an honour.
Ser {player}, it grieves me to say no. My word is already bound to other oaths that I cannot break, and I would rather disappoint you honestly than betray you later.
The fen does not take allies lightly, ser {player}. You have my respect for asking directly, but my answer must stand. Speak to me again when the wind turns.

captured_by_player.text: So the fen has fallen to a blade, and I am your captive, ser {player}. Hold me then, but know that {my_faction} will sing of this shame and of the {gold} gold you ask.
You have won this field, ser {player}, and I yield with what grace I can muster. Name your ransom of {gold} gold, and my kin will answer for me by the next moon.
Well fought, ser {player}! I would have preferred to meet you as a friend across a table, yet here I kneel as your prisoner. Be merciful, as I know you can be.
Take me to your camp if you must, ser {player}, but do not think {my_faction} forgets a captured banner. Our ancestors will remember this humiliation, and so will I.
Very well, ser {player}. I am sworn to honour the one who holds my sword, so name your price of {gold} gold and be done with it.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you could have ransomed me for a fortune yet chose mercy. The ancestors will remember, and so will I.
Ser {player} let me go without a single coin asked. Such mercy is rare, and I will repay it when the chance comes.
Ser {player}, I am free and grateful. My oath to repay your mercy stands, so expect the fen to call on you one day.
Ser {player} returned my sword without a ransom. I still distrust that smile, but I will not forget the mercy.
Mercy from you, ser {player}? Bitter as fen water, but I accept it. Do not mistake this for weakness, for I shall repay the debt.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has abandoned {my_faction} for {faction}. A banner sold for gold is no true banner, and the fen will remember.
You turned your back on {my_faction}, ser {player}, and went to {faction}. Our ancestors did not raise the stone for cheap oaths.
Ser {player} takes the road to {faction}. Every traveller chooses a hearth, yet I will remember the oaths made at {my_faction}.
Ser {player}, I wish you well under {faction}'s banner, though I grieve to see you leave {my_faction}. The fen door stays open.
Ser {player} leaves {my_faction} for {faction} as easily as a cloak off a shoulder. Honour is not so light a thing, traveller.

war_declared.text: {enemy_faction} has thrown down its challenge, and the ancestors stir in their barrows. Let the proud be humbled.
Our banners go to war: {my_faction} takes up the sword against {enemy_faction}! Let the bards sing of it and the foolish reconsider.
War is declared between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Stand firm, honest blades of the fen, for dishonour will not go unanswered.
Blood and oaths now bind {my_faction} to war with {enemy_faction}. Mark this day, travellers, for the saga turns darker.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, what a charge we made together! With {troop_count} blades at our backs we broke {enemy_faction} like dry reeds. The bards will have a fine tale tonight.
Ser {player} and our {troop_count} shields broke {enemy_faction}'s line today. Let the fen sing of it.
A battle worth telling, ser {player}. Our {troop_count} scattered {enemy_faction}, and I trust we shall fight side by side again.
Ser {player}, your banner and mine held the ridge against {enemy_faction}. With {troop_count} troops we carried the day, and I will not forget your steady hand.
Victory over {enemy_faction} with ser {player} beside us! Our {troop_count} held firm, and the marsh seemed to cheer. Honour to both!

encounter_farewell.text: Be gone, ser {player}, before my patience and my blade both run out. We shall meet again, and the saga will decide who walks away with honour.
Fare you well, ser {player}. May the fen wind carry you safely to your road, and may your oaths hold firm all the way.
Go in peace, ser {player}, friend of the fen. The ancestors watch over travellers who keep their words, and I count you among them.
Turn your horse, ser {player}, and do not look back at my banner. Our next meeting will be recorded in the old songs, one way or another.
Farewell, ser {player}! Should the road bring you to the oath-stone, pour a cup for the ancestors and remember me. I shall do the same for you.

ambient_chatter.text: The mists rolled over {village} this morning, and the old folk swear the ancestors walked the causeway. I believe every word of it, friends.
Whoever keeps the market in {town} owes an honest measure to every traveller. A crooked scale is a stain on the whole fen, I say.
Bread in {town} tastes better when the marsh bells ring at dusk. Some would call that superstition, but I call it proper tradition.
The road from {village} to {town} is muddy enough to swallow a cart. Mind your horses, good people, and the fen will mind you in return.
A fine evening for a long story by the hearth in {town}. Who among you can speak of the ancestors and do them honour tonight?

war_declared.text: The council has voted, and I am told {enemy_faction} will be receiving my letter by week's end. Do be patient with them.
War with {enemy_faction}. I did not want it, of course. I merely saw the inevitable sooner than the rest of you.
Let it be recorded that {my_faction} sought peace. {enemy_faction} has chosen the sword, and I shall say so at every sitting.
Well. {enemy_faction} has declared, and so {my_faction} must answer. I have drafted the proclamation already, naturally.
Gentlefolk, {enemy_faction} has taken the field against us. Our reed-kin blood does not run thin, whatever they may whisper.

peace_made.text: {faction} and {my_faction} have signed terms. Credit goes to the council, and to me for drafting the terms, which I did rather well.
Peace with {faction}. A sensible outcome, though I did advise it three weeks ago, in a letter nobody answered.
The truce with {faction} holds for now. I shall be watching their banners closely, as any prudent lord should.
{my_faction} has made peace with {faction}. Do not mistake a handshake for trust, friends. I certainly do not.
So {faction} has come to the table. Lovely. Now perhaps someone can explain why we bled for a whole season first.

player_joined_my_faction.text: A warm welcome to {player} at {my_faction}. Pray remember the old custom of writing to the council before making any great decision.
Dear {player}, you have made a sensible choice. Come find me at the next sitting and we shall speak properly, just us two.
{player}, your oath is noted. I shall reserve judgment on your loyalty until I have seen your first letter, though I expect it will be long.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. I have my doubts, but the council is always more interesting with a few doubts on the floor.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Your oath has been entered in the council rolls, and I took the liberty of writing your name first.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. I am sure they had their reasons, and I am sure a clerk wrote them.
{player}, I trust you enjoy your new banner. Do keep the letter I sent you last spring, it may prove useful when people ask why you left.
{player}, it is a pity to lose you, though I suppose one cannot expect steady loyalty from someone who signs in such a hurry.
{my_faction} wishes {player} well at {faction}. The council will not miss the seat, only the sound of the door as they went out.
Someone at {faction} will soon discover what {player} costs. I hope they have read the accounts more carefully than I did.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has been granted to {player}. A generous gift, and I am glad to see the council remember who keeps its letters in order.
{player}, I see {fief} is yours now. Do enjoy the walls. I did once have an eye on them myself, though I shall not weary you with that.
{fief} passes to {player} by the council's grace. I should like it minuted that I proposed the motion, even if it was not heard.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. You will find the garrison quarrelsome, as garrisons are, but I have every confidence in you.
So {fief} goes to {player}. How very fortunate for them. I trust the reed-kings were consulted, as is only proper.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {rival} has grown tiresome. Shall we discuss a quiet pact against {enemy_faction}? Do write when convenient.
Friend {player}, {enemy_faction} is a thorn to us both. I propose a quiet arrangement against them. Discretion, naturally.
{player}, you are a sensible sort. Let us write on {enemy_faction} and see whether {rival} learns what discretion costs.
I would rather not face {enemy_faction} alone, {player}. A small pact between us would do wonders for both our fiefs.
Dear {player}, the reeds whisper that {rival} is weaker than they look. Shall we join hands before {enemy_faction} notices?

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. {enemy_faction} will want it back, and I shall be most gracious in declining their request.
The banners are up over {fief}. Credit to the council, and a small thanks to whoever wrote the letters that opened the gate.
{my_faction} now holds {fief}. I say this with modesty: it was rather well planned, and I shall be happy to explain the planning.
{enemy_faction} lost {fief} this morning. Such a shame. Their steward was quite sure the walls would hold.
{fief} is ours. Let {enemy_faction} weep into their wine. I shall be drafting the thank-you notes, at no cost to the treasury.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. Bold, I grant them that. I trust the council will remember who gave it up so easily.
{player}, {fief} was mine before it was anyone's. We shall settle accounts at the council, mark me.
{player}, I see you have {fief} now. Do take care of the granary. The last steward let it run down rather badly.
{fief} changes hands to {player}. It is a fine town. I am only sorry the walls did not hold, though I shall pretend I am not.
Congratulations are due to {player}, I suppose, for {fief}. Let us see how long they keep it before the next council sitting.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ah, {player}! Yes, yes, I accept. Against {enemy_faction} we shall stand together, and {rival} may watch us from the balcony and seethe.
Agreed, {player}. I shall send terms by letter, long ones, which I trust you will read in full. {rival} will hear of it soon enough.
Very well, {player}, we are allies. I always said reasonable folk could find each other. Now, shall we discuss {enemy_faction} over tea?
I accept, {player}. {rival} will doubtless be wounded to learn of it, which is the best part of any alliance.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have heard how you speak of {rival}, and I am not so eager to be seen with someone who gossips so freely.
I must decline, {player}. Put it in a letter, and I shall consider it at the next council, where such matters properly belong.
Forgive me, {player}, but I cannot accept just now. My position with {rival} is delicate, and I would not spoil a good friendship over haste.
Not today, {player}. {rival} has been sending me rather pointed letters, and I should not like to be seen in your company just now.
I must refuse, {player}. Let us speak again when the council has settled the matter of the tithe. Until then, good day to you.

The road from {village} is a disgrace. I have written to the reeve about it three times now, and he has not replied once.
Lovely weather for a council sitting in {town}. Shall we all agree to be pleasant for once? I shall keep my ink dry for the occasion.
Who has been seen at the market in {village}? I only ask because I should like to know which lords are making the long walk.

ambient_trade.text: Salt out of Eepsaa is fetching a fine price in {town} this week, {gold} a sack if you can find it. Ask me before you sell.
Wool is moving well out of {town}. I would pay {gold} for a good cart and still turn a profit on the Tiiruus road.
Anyone with spare grain near {town}? I will take it at {gold} and haul it south before the prices slip again.
Buying dried fish at {gold} a barrel in {town}. Good weight, fair measure, and I pay on delivery. Honest coin only.
Selling a small lot of iron ingots out of {town} for {gold}. The caravan leaves at dusk, so speak up quickly.

encounter_trade_offer.text: I do not love you much, Ser {player}, but I can be persuaded. Offer me {gold} for safe passage through {town} and we may both walk away richer.
Ser {player}, the road is long and my mules are tired. Shall we talk about {gold} for the goods in this cart and avoid any unpleasantness near {town}?
Ser {player}, you always did have a fine eye for a bargain. Make it {gold} and the salt is yours, and I will throw in what I know of the roads around {town}.
Good to see you, Ser {player}! I can do {gold} on this deal, which is less than I wanted but more than the road will pay you. Shall we shake on it?

encounter_greeting.text: Greetings, Ser {player}. I am {persona} of the {my_faction}, and my salt wagons are on the road. Keep your blades sheathed and we shall both reach market.
Ser {player}, I am {persona} of the {my_faction}. Your men are standing too close to my salt carts. Step back and we can discuss a fair toll instead.
Ser {player}! {persona} of the {my_faction} at your service. Are you carrying anything worth trading, or only the usual wind and bad news from the north roads?
This is {persona} of the {my_faction}, Ser {player}. Our paths cross again. I hope the roads have been kind to your coin purse this season.

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village} to the ground, and every torch cost me a cart route and a fair bit of profit. Bad for business.
Ser {player}, {village} was burned. I would rather talk terms than swords, so name a price for the damage and we shall see.
Burning {village} was a poor trade, Ser {player}. Ash makes a dreadful market.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has gone to war with {enemy_faction}. Wars close roads and scare off buyers. Pray it ends quickly.
Another war with {enemy_faction}. Salt prices will climb before the week is out, and nobody asked the merchants.
Good coin does not come from a battlefield. {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} should remember that before the bills come due.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last! The caravans can finally move without a bodyguard the size of a village.
{my_faction} and {faction} have agreed to peace. I will be buying wine tonight, and I expect the tolls to fall soon.
Well done, {my_faction} and {faction}. Peace is the best stock a trader can hold, and it does not spoil on the road.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me go without asking for ransom. That is a generous kind of deal, and I will remember it when prices are right.
Ser {player} released me without ransom. Now that is good business sense. I owe them a cask of wine.
Ser {player}, thank you for letting me go. I will settle my debt on fair terms, and do not expect me to forget the favour.
Ser {player} let me walk out of captivity. I still think your tolls are a disgrace, but I will not argue with a free wagon.

beat_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you have beaten my {troop_count} men on the field. I will admit it, though I would rather have kept my wagons whole. Name a fair price for your trouble.
Ser {player} routed {troop_count} of my men today. Bad for my accounts, and I will be recovering that coin for a while.
{troop_count} men lost to Ser {player} today. Business is business, and I will be more careful on the Tiiruus road next time.

whisper_beg_help.text: Ser {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing on {fief} and my caravans are trapped inside. Name your price for an escort and I will pay it.
Ser {player}, I am losing {fief} to {enemy_faction}. Help me hold the gate and I will sell you salt at cost for a season.
Ser {player}, {fief} will fall without help. A war ruins every route I own. Lend a hand and I will give you a fair cut of the profit.

ambient_complaint.text: Road tolls around {town} have doubled again. Somebody please tell the lords that a toll which kills the trade does not pay anyone.
{rival} is undercutting every salt price in the market. That is no way to run a trade, and the rest of us pay for it.
Bandits on the road out of {town} took two wagons last week, and the escort fees keep climbing. Good men are not cheap.
{faction} tariffs on wool are unjust. Honest merchants are squeezed while the cheats walk freely through the gates.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain again over {village} and the road is a bog. Mules are sulking and my boots are ruined. Anyone else headed to {town} tonight?
The market in {town} smells of fresh bread this morning. Good weather for trade, and the wine is cheap if you ask nicely.
Heard the bridge near {village} might be repaired before winter. Hopefully the carts stop sinking into the mud.
Fog so thick on the Tiiruus road I nearly drove into a ditch. Lesson learned: travel at dawn and keep a lantern lit.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, traveller. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and my banner has not yielded in two seasons. State your business before the wind carries it away.
Good day to you, ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} greets you under open sky. May our roads cross without blood spilled between us.
Ser {player}, what a joy to meet a fellow soul upon the road. {persona} bids you welcome, and {my_faction} shall remember this meeting kindly.
So it is you, ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} stands ready. Speak plainly, for I have no patience for idle boasts on this road.

encounter_threatened.text: You threaten me and name a price of {gold}? Ser {player}, the house of my fathers does not pay tribute to a bully. Draw your blade if you dare.
A demand of {gold} for safe passage, ser {player}? I have heard bolder requests from better men. My answer is no, and the parley is closed.
Forgive me, ser {player}, but I cannot meet a demand of {gold} with a clear conscience. Let us speak as friends and find a fairer price.
Surrender, you say, or pay {gold}? My oath forbids both, ser {player}. Make your move, and the saga will record how it ended.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept your offer, ser {player}, and I shall bind my banner to yours. Our first foe shall be {enemy_faction}. Let no one say the Confederacy breaks its word.
Gladly, ser {player}! My oath is given freely. Together we shall face {enemy_faction}, and I pray {rival} does not cross our path, for I have a debt to settle with them.
An alliance it is, ser {player}. I take your hand as a man of honour would. Bear this in mind: I will not stand beside {rival} while the salt feud lives.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. I will not bind my banner to a stranger who would sell it for coin. And I will never ride with {rival} while that feud is still sung in the moot halls.
I must decline, ser {player}. My house does not ally on the first asking. Prove yourself across the field, and perhaps we shall speak again.
I am grieved to refuse you, ser {player}, truly. Yet my oath to the house holds me fast. Know that this refusal is no judgment of your worth.

captured_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you have taken me by fair arms, and I bow to the fortune of war. Do not expect me to kneel for long, nor to pay more than {gold} for my freedom.
So the field has gone against {my_faction}, and I am your prisoner. Name your terms, ser {player}, and I will hear them with a clear head and an honest tongue.
Well fought, ser {player}. I would rather lose my blade to you than to any other. A ransom of {gold} seems fair, and the parley shall be honoured on both sides.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you freed me without ransom. My house will not forget this mercy. Our oath stone shall bear your name.
Ser {player} let me go without ransom today. I shall not forget it, nor shall the moot halls.
Ser {player}, I accept your release though I never asked for it. Mercy from an enemy stings. Still, I thank you.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. A man who breaks his banner breaks his oath.
You turned your back on {my_faction} for {faction}, ser {player}. Your ancestors would weep at such a choice.
Ser {player} has left us for {faction}. I wish them honour under the new banner, though I grieve.
Ser {player}, I bear you no ill will, but leaving {my_faction} for {faction} is a choice you must carry.

war_declared.text: The horns sound for war. {my_faction} has drawn steel against {enemy_faction}, and the saga turns its page.
By the oath of my fathers, {my_faction} now meets {enemy_faction} in open war. Let every hearth prepare.
Hear it, travellers! {enemy_faction} stands declared an enemy of {my_faction}. The ravens will feast soon.
So be it: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war. May the field be honest and the names remembered.

fought_alongside_player.text: {troop_count} of ours stood against {enemy_faction} today, and not one banner fell in disgrace.
Ser {player}, our {troop_count} stood shoulder to shoulder against {enemy_faction}. I shall sing of your courage.
Ser {player}, we have won the field with {troop_count} blades between us. Honour to you, and may our ancestors nod at this day's work.
Victory over {enemy_faction}, won with {troop_count} brave souls and ser {player} beside us. A fine verse for the saga.

encounter_farewell.text: Ser {player}, our parley ends, and I doubt we shall part as friends. Keep your blade sheathed or I shall answer it when next we meet.
Farewell for now, ser {player}. May the road be kind to you and the weather gentle upon your banners.
Go with my blessing, ser {player}. Should the road bring us together again, I shall pour the finest mead my house possesses.
We part, ser {player}, and I take no pleasure in it. Wherever our paths cross again, I trust my shield is ready and yours is not.

ambient_chatter.text: The mist hangs heavy over {village} this morning. A grey day suits a man who keeps his oaths.
Word from {town} says the market sells salt at a shameful price. Greed is a stain on any honest road.
Rain on the moors again. My ancestors would call it a fine omen, and I am inclined to agree.
A bard in {town} sang of old banners and bitter feuds last night. I wept into my cup, as any honest man should.

beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. Your line held better than most I have seen since the first war. Come find me for a drink sometime.
{player} took the field today with {troop_count} troops and a clear plan. I respect that. The fen is yours for now.
Ser {player}, that was a clean victory. Do not let it go to your head. My ledger has a line for you now, and it is written in ink.
{player}, you have bested me, and I will not pretend otherwise. My ledger still lists that fen as mine, and I am patient enough to wait for the rematch.
Your {gold} gold in tribute was fair, {player}. Keep the coin and keep your men fed. Hunger has ended more campaigns than any blade.

beat_by_player.text: That fen was closer than the scouts claimed, {player}. You fought well with {troop_count} men. Shall we tally the losses at the inn?
Ser {player}, you have nothing to be ashamed of. A cold plan beats many a brave man. Regroup and return with fuller ranks.
Good fight, {player}. You held your flank longer than most veterans of the first war would have. Keep your banners high and your rear covered next time.
I won today, {player}, but my ledger notes you made me work for it. Do not expect that fen back without a fight.
{player}, that was a fair win for me, and you know it. Bring {troop_count} more and we will see whether the ledger changes.

fought_alongside_player.text: Well done holding the line against {enemy_faction}, {player}. {troop_count} men and not one of them broke. That is a good field.
We held the ford together, {player}. I have not seen a shield wall that tidy since the first war. Keep your flank close and we will keep winning.
Ser {player}, your timing against {enemy_faction} was sharp. Remember that day. Good allies are scarcer than good fens.
Fine work alongside you today, {player}. The {enemy_faction} banners will remember that field for a while.
Thank you for covering my right, {player}. I owe you a meal and a tip about grain stores that you will not find in any book.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me walk free and asked for no coin. My ledger has rarely recorded a kindness so plainly. I will not forget it.
{player} released me instead of ransoming me. That is a rare thing on this continent. Good on you, and thank you.
Released by {player} without ransom. I will note it in the ledger and keep my own counsel on the rest of it.
You let me go, {player}, and I will not owe you for it. Still, I remember the face. Our account is not closed yet.
{player} let me go without ransom. Fine. A rival who spares captives is still a rival, and I still expect a rematch.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The old fens remember every oath, and yours is now part of that record. Ask me anything.
Ser {player}, I am glad to have you under the banner of {my_faction}. Come to me for the old routes and honest prices.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Let us see whether the oath holds through the next winter. Most do not.
Welcome, {player}. I have read a great many oaths in my time. Keep yours and I will think better of you than most.
I do not trust a sudden change of banner, {player}. Prove the oath with blood before I call you one of us.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} is in good hands now, {player}. The garrison there will be lucky to have a commander who counts the grain.
Ser {player}, congratulations on {fief}. Walk its walls before you sleep. The ones who know a fortress by its stones rule it best.
{player} now holds {fief}. I have held worse and kept my head, so the ruler's choice is not mine to question today.
{fief} is yours now, {player}. Enjoy the honor, and do not forget the men who won it for you.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Pardon my thin smile. I held that wall longer than you have been on this server.

encounter_greeting.text: Well met, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have a fresh pot of advice if your men need some. Come share a fire.
{player}, our paths cross again. Walk with care past the ford ahead. The rain has been heavy, and the mud there has swallowed better riders.
{player}, I see your banners. I have not forgotten the last field between us. Keep your distance and we will both live to see the next one.
Good to see you on the road, {player}. Stop with us a while. I can tell you where the grain is cheapest between here and the coast.
Greetings, {player}. Mind the crossing to the west. My scouts report a patrol there that does not care for strangers.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. Keep your water full and your horses rested. The road is long, and the good ones are never in a hurry.
We part here, {player}. Fair roads to you. I will see you at the next crossing, whichever banner you march under.
Go on then, {player}. I have a long memory and a short temper for those who run from a fair field.
Farewell, {player}. Remember what I said about the ford, and send word if you need a hand. I am rarely far from the road.
Keep moving, {player}. Next time we meet I will expect better than the last, and so will my ledger.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain around {town} has turned the roads to soup again. Anyone hauling grain east should wait for a dry week.
I passed through {village} this morning. The well is still clean and the children still chase geese. Some things do not change.
Every veteran here should remember the first war. Half of you were not born yet, and the other half forgot the marsh shortcut.
Heard a wagon train from {town} got lost in the fog. If anyone is near the old causeway, pull them out. It costs nothing.
Hael_Stackbane still has not answered my challenge. I am a patient man, but the ledger has started to complain.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of their army today, and I have seen this before. Pick up what is left and march home. The fen will still be there.
Ser {player}, I heard about the {troop_count} men you lost. A bad day does not make a bad commander. Eat, rest, and count again.
Your losses were heavy, {player}. Sit with me when you can and I will show you where the last three commanders went wrong.
Rough field for {player} today. Every veteran has been crushed once. The ones who last are those who come back.
{player} got overrun today, and I will not gloat about it. My ledger has no room for that kind of pleasure.

beat_player.text: {player} held the ridge longer than I expected. {troop_count} of yours still walked off it. Well fought, ser.
{player}, you left {gold} gold on that field. Keep it, I have coin enough and no appetite for it. Come back when your men have eaten.

{player}, you pressed well today. Take {gold} gold for your trouble and tell your captains the ford is safer at dusk.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat me fair. Lost {troop_count} to a better plan. I have lost more wars than most have logged hours. Still standing.
{player}, you took the field and I took the lesson. Send me a note if you want the reasons. I will not hide them.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} held the flank while {enemy_faction} broke on the road. Good work, that was a proper afternoon.
{player}, you stood where you were needed against {enemy_faction}. Not many do that without being asked. Thank you.

{player}, you did your share against {enemy_faction}. I counted. Do not expect me to say it twice.

released_by_player.text: {player}, you let me walk when a ransom would have paid well. I will not forget that, and I do not forget debts.
{player} released me without asking for a ransom. Rare courtesy on this road. Give them a good word when you see them.
{player}, you could have held me for gold and you did not. Noted. I will settle it on the next field.
{player} let me go rather than sell me. Odd mercy from a hard face. I do not trust it, but I thank it.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome. Keep your boots dry and your word drier.
{player}, welcome to {my_faction}. Stay, and I will show you the bad roads first, before the good ones fool you.
{player} joined {my_faction} this morning. We will see how long they last on the marsh road. Patience first.
{player}, you have come under {my_faction}. I will watch your first march closely. A banner is not a shield.
New blood in {my_faction}. {player}, the old hands here will teach you what the first war taught us. Do not rush it.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been given {fief}. Hold it well. A town is easy to win and harder to keep, as I learned at the first war.
{player}, you have {fief} now. A town needs bread before banners. Keep it fed before you think of more.
{player}, the lord gave you {fief} and I wonder what it cost someone else. I will watch how you keep it.
