{player}, {fief} is a fine place. I am glad it fell to someone who will not sell the granary. Congratulations, ser.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Our parties meet on a poor road. Water your horses and we can talk a while.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Your men look tired, and so do mine. Rest the column before we speak of anything else.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Step aside from the ford and we have nothing to say. Do not make me repeat it.
Well met, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have seen worse roads than this one. Ride safe, the marsh is close.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I have held this road before without drawing steel. Say your piece and keep your hands off the reins.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe road, {player}. Mind the marsh edge after dusk, it has taken better riders than either of us.
That will do for today, {player}. Keep your column tight and your torches lit.
We are done, {player}. Keep riding, and do not come back to this ford unless you have a better argument.
Go well, {player}. Come find me at the old waystone if you want the story of the first war.
Farewell, {player}. Good talk, if a short one.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. The road to {village} will be mud until the thaw. Pack an extra cloak.
Lost half a wagon to the bog outside {village} last night. Keep to the stones, friends.
Someone asked me today if the old walls of {town} still stand. They do, and so do the men who built them.
The marsh fog is thick over the road to {village}. Keep your lanterns lit and your tempers low.
Late grain carts out of {town}. Mind your rations, the roads are long this season.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men in one bad morning. It happens to the best of us. Sit down, get some bread, and try again.

{player} got caught on open ground and lost {troop_count} men. Nothing new on this road, but the lesson is still there.
{player}, {troop_count} men gone and no one to blame but the ground you chose. I will not gloat, but I noticed.

Good day, traveller. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Let it be written that our paths crossed on this road, and that we met as honourable folk.
Ser {player}, what a joy to see your banner upon this road! {persona} of {my_faction} greets you with a full heart, friend.

encounter_threatened.text: Pay you {gold}? Such a sum would shame the mourners of my house. Withdraw, ser {player}, while your honour remains intact.

Ser {player}, I know you jest, for no friend of mine would bargain for {gold} on a road of grief. Let us speak of it over bread.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept your offer. Upon the blood of my ancestors I pledge my banner beside yours against {enemy_faction}. Let us prove the pact in the field.
Ser {player}, a pact with you warms the heart! Together we shall break the banners of {enemy_faction}, and the rolls will sing of it for generations.
I shall not share a road with {rival}, but your word, ser {player}, I find sound. Let our banners fly together against {enemy_faction}.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. I will not bind my banner to one who speaks lightly of the dead. Find another hand to hold.
I must decline, ser {player}. My house cannot ally while {rival} still walks the roads I am sworn to guard. Forgive my caution.
It grieves me to refuse you, dear friend. My ancestors would not forgive a pact made in haste, so let us speak again when the road is kinder.

captured_by_player.text: So, ser {player}, you have taken my blade and my freedom. Hold me well, for {my_faction} will not forget the hand that bound me. Name your ransom, if you dare.
A captive of {my_faction}, I am, ser {player}. Your ransom of {gold} is steep, yet I shall not beg. Let the terms be spoken plainly.
Ser {player}, a fair victory and a gentle chain. I bear you no grudge for your hand in this. Speak your terms and we shall see them settled with honour.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you loosed my chains. I owe you no thanks, yet my house shall remember this mercy, bitter as it is.
Ser {player} released me rather than sell my freedom for gold. This shall be written in the rolls of Gaiuuk.
Ser {player}, your mercy has not gone unnoticed. Had you taken my ransom I would have grieved. Instead I am in your debt, friend.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction}. Let the rolls of Gaiuuk record this betrayal of {my_faction}.
Ser {player}, you have chosen {faction} over {my_faction}. I shall not curse your name, but the road ahead will be hard. Go with care.
Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Oaths bend in the wind, and I wish them well upon whatever road they walk now.
Ser {player}, my heart is heavy at your parting from {my_faction}, yet I know your reasons are your own. Go with an honest oath.

war_declared.text: Let it be written that {my_faction} has taken up the sword against {enemy_faction}. May the dead on both sides be honoured.
The banners are raised: {my_faction} now stands in war against {enemy_faction}. Let every mourner of the realm take note.
I grieve this war between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}, though my oath demands I stand with my kin. Let the dead be named in full.

fought_alongside_player.text: Victory over {enemy_faction}, won beside ser {player} and {troop_count} brave souls! The rolls shall sing of this field.
Ser {player}, your shield beside mine turned the day. I shall name each of the {troop_count} who stood with us at my house's vigil.
Ser {player}, we stood together against {enemy_faction}, and I remain standing with {troop_count} of my own. Your arm was true and I shall not forget it.
Ser {player}, we have shed blood together against {enemy_faction}, and the dead of both our banners shall be honoured. My ancestors would approve of such a comrade, friend.

encounter_farewell.text: We part, ser {player}, but I have not forgotten your insolence. May the road take you far from my banner, and may our next meeting be less kind to you.
Farewell, ser {player}. May your road be dry and your oaths be kept. Our paths shall cross again upon this wide land.

ambient_chatter.text: The fog hangs thick over {village} this morning, and the mourners' bells ring slow for the lost. Keep your lanterns lit, travellers.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have had four carts bled dry by your sort on this road. Keep your distance and we shall both keep our purses.
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here, with salt and wool on the cart and a sharp eye on the road. Anything you want to buy or sell before we part ways?
Ser {player}! {persona} of {my_faction} at your service. The road has been quiet and my carts are full, so if you have goods to move, we should talk before the next toll gate.

{player}, burning {village} cost me two carts and a week of contracts. Name a price to stop and I'd sooner pay than fight.
Word is {village} went up in smoke. Bad for business on every road, and bad for anyone wanting a fair price on salt this season.
{player}, I have not decided if you are a reaver or simply a poor planner. Tell me which, and perhaps we can still do business.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. Roads will close, prices will jump, and every honest cart will pay for it.
War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Somebody tell the generals that wool does not weave itself in a siege.
{enemy_faction} and {my_faction} at war again. I have three caravans sitting idle and a lot of salt going soft.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction}, finally. The toll roads will open and my carts can breathe again.
{my_faction} has made peace with {faction}. Good news for the wool trade and for every farmer who likes to keep his barn full.
Terms are signed between {my_faction} and {faction}. With luck the bandits will have less excuse to hide in the reeds.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me walk instead of ransoming me. Remember that, because my next salt cart to you comes at cost.
Released by {player} without ransom. Fair play, and I will not forget it when the next toll ledger is drawn up.
{player} released me rather than ask a ransom. Odd sort of mercy, but I will take the cart back and count the rest as a loss.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat my men at the ford with {troop_count} of their own. Lost a whole cart to it, but I will sell the horses anyway.
{player}, {troop_count} of your men broke my line today. Well fought. Shall we settle the cost of the losses over a cup of wine?
Ser {player}, {troop_count} blades and you still left me standing. A good fight costs both of us, so let us talk terms on the horses before we part.
Ser {player}, you beat me with {troop_count} men and I will not pretend otherwise. But the road is still open to traders, and I will pay for it.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing {fief} and my coffers are thin. Send men if you can spare them and I will pay in salt.
{player}, {fief} is under threat from {enemy_faction}. I know this is bad for business, so name a fair figure to help us hold it.

{player}, I hate to ask. {enemy_faction} is grinding down {fief} and I cannot afford to lose it. Name your terms and I will listen.

{rival} is undercutting every salt merchant in {town}. Not fair dealing, that, and it is ruining the price for everybody.

Anyone else lagging badly around {village}? My cart is stuck halfway across a ford and the map is not loading properly.

Fog rolling off the marsh near {village} this morning. Good cover for a caravan, bad cover for a man with a map.

war_declared.text: The council of {my_faction} has spoken on {enemy_faction}. I merely moved the motion. The blades will do the rest.
Let it be minuted that {my_faction} did not seek this war. {enemy_faction} simply forgot to read the charter.
{enemy_faction} was given three chances to be reasonable. I have counted them all, and so has the council.
Grievances, once tabled, have a way of becoming campaigns. {my_faction} is only following procedure, as ever.

peace_made.text: {my_faction} and {faction} have agreed terms. A pleasant outcome, though I confess I had hoped for a slightly longer quarrel.
The truce with {faction} is signed, and I shall be the first to say I drafted the clauses.
Peace with {faction} is a fine thing for the ledgers. Do try not to mistake a pause for a permanent arrangement.
{my_faction} has made its peace with {faction}. The council will meet next week to decide who gets the credit.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. I do hope you find the council's benches comfortable. They are rarely kind to newcomers.
I see you have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Wise, I think. Do let us discuss your ambitions over a quiet word soon.
{player} now sits under the banner of {my_faction}. How brave. The council will watch with interest to see how long it lasts.
Your oath to {my_faction} is a fine decision, {player}. I have already drafted a seat for you on the next council.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. A bold move. I am sure the council will minute it with great sorrow.
I notice you have taken your oaths to {faction}, {player}. Do not worry, I shall not table the matter. Yet.
Changing banners is hardly a crime, {player}, though I would have preferred to hear it from you first, over tea.
So {player} prefers {faction} to {my_faction}. Truly, I am only noting the change in seating arrangements.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} now answers to {player}. A splendid appointment, and one the council endorsed with barely a dissenting voice.
So {fief} has gone to you, {player}. I do hope the duties suit your talents. The ledgers are rather unforgiving.
{player} has been granted {fief}. I shall reserve my applause until I have read the accounts for the first season.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Should you need allies on the council to keep it, you know where to find me.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {rival} has been courting {enemy_faction} behind the council's back. I would rather we dealt with that together.
A word of caution, {player}. {rival} speaks warmly of you in public and quite differently elsewhere. Shall we compare notes?
Join me against {enemy_faction}, {player}, and we shall see {rival} lose the next vote. I can promise you the seat.
There is little love lost between us and {rival}, {player}. An alliance against {enemy_faction} would serve us both nicely.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. {enemy_faction} will call it a raid. The council will call it a mandate.
The banners of {my_faction} now fly over {fief}, taken from {enemy_faction}. Motion carried, and well carried.
{fief} is ours, and {enemy_faction} may wonder how a single vote cost them a castle. I shall not explain.
Let the record show {my_faction} holds {fief}. I drafted the resolution, so I am obliged to be pleased.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. A tidy piece of work, if one overlooks the gaps in the defences I was promised.
{fief} is yours now, {player}. Enjoy it. I have a long memory and a longer list of motions.
Well taken, {player}. {fief} was never quite the jewel I described to the council. Do keep the walls in good repair.
So {player} has marched into {fief}. The council will want an inquiry. I shall be delighted to chair it.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Agreed, {player}. Let us strike at {rival} while {enemy_faction} is still busy counting its coin. I will draft the terms.
Your offer is accepted, {player}. {rival} has annoyed too many people, and I am only too happy to be the one who says so.
Very well, {player}, we ally. {enemy_faction} will hardly expect the two of us to agree on anything, which is precisely the charm.
I accept, {player}. Mind {rival} does not hear of it before the council does. Such things have a way of leaking.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have seen how you treat your allies. I would sooner trust {rival} with my purse, and that is saying something.
I must decline, {player}. The council is not yet persuaded, and {rival} would take it poorly. Perhaps another season.
Regretfully no, {player}. Your offer is generous, but {rival} holds a seat I need, and I cannot be seen to tear it up yet.
Not today, {player}. Let us see how the next vote goes before we bind ourselves to anyone, least of all {rival}.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} has made the council benches damp and the members damper. Motion to adjourn, I think.
Has anyone else heard the fishermen of {village} are petitioning for a new dock? Excellent. Another item for the agenda.
The roads from {village} to {town} are a disgrace. I shall raise the matter, and then I shall raise it again.
Heard the market in {town} is quiet this week. Quiet markets make for quiet councils, which suits me well enough.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Ask me about the crossings and the old roads, and I will tell you what I can.
Ser {player}, I am glad to have you with {my_faction}. Listen more than you speak in the early skirmishes. That is how I learned.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Let us see what the new blood can do. The good recruits always listened first.
Ser {player}, {my_faction} takes you on, though I want to see your oath proven before I believe it. Prove yourself where it counts.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been given {fief}. A fine choice. I hope the walls hold better than mine did in the second siege.
Ser {player}, {fief} is a heavy gift. Walls do not hold themselves, and I have seen good men lose towns to a dry well.
So {player} gets {fief}. I held the fen crossing since the first war with spades alone, and nobody wrote me a song. Good luck.
Ser {player}, I am proud to see {fief} in good hands. If you need advice on drainage or weak ground, you know where to find me.

encounter_greeting.text: Good day, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}. Mind the fen road ahead, the ground is soft and it has swallowed better horses than yours.
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here. I have walked this road since before your banners were stitched, so I will keep my eyes open.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I would rather not spend a morning on you, but I will if I must. Stand aside and we may both keep our men.
{player}! {persona} of {my_faction} again. It is good to see a familiar banner out here. How are the roads treating you these days?

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. May the fen mud stay out of your boots and the sinkholes stay where you can see them.
We will part here, {player}. The northern ford is shallower than the map says, and I would not trust the bridge at dusk.
Go on then, {player}. Our paths will cross again, and when they do I expect the same firm handshake you gave my scouts. Good day.
Until the next crossing, {player}. Take a little care on the wet road, and do not let a bit of mud spoil a good ride.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the fen again. Every spring some young rider tries the road to {town} and learns the hard way it is not a road at all.
Has anyone seen the herders from {village} this morning? Their flock was grazing near the ditch and I would hate to see a sheep go in.
Grain in {town} is climbing again. Buy what you can carry now, because the next dry spell will hit the stalls before the carts do.
I have been asked again about the tunnel under the old walls. No, I will not give directions, but the mortar was soft that year.
Good sunrise over the marsh this morning. A man could forget the wars for an hour if he did not know what the mud was hiding.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the causeway today. Regroup and come back. The mud forgives everyone eventually.
Ser {player}, I saw what happened to your {troop_count} men. I lost two armies in the first war and still came back. You will too.
A bad day for {player}, with {troop_count} lost. The rest of us have had them, so do not let the loud ones tell you otherwise.
Ser {player}, {troop_count} men gone is a poor showing. Look hard at where your line broke before you march out again.

beat_player.text: {player} lost the flank with {troop_count} men on the field. the ratio was never in question. gg
{player} your reserves sat idle for the whole second phase. {troop_count} men wasted. fix that before the rematch
you fought well for the numbers you had. {troop_count} against my line was never going to hold. next time bring a second formation and we will see
{gold} in mercenary upkeep to hold that field. not a sustainable trade for you. check your ledger
{troop_count} men at a 3 to 1 disadvantage on open ground and you still lost the flank. the numbers are not subjective

beat_by_player.text: my archers were out of position. the rest of the line was fine. {player} took the flank cleanly and i will not argue it
{player} you took {troop_count} men through my center at the wrong angle. i will have the numbers on it by tonight. expect the rematch
{player} your cavalry timing was clean. i was watching the wrong flank for two minutes and that was the whole fight. {troop_count} of mine broke because of it
fair result. you read the line better than i expected. i still think the ratio favoured me going in, but your second wave was correct
lost to {player} with {troop_count} still in the field. a loss from a bad formation is still a loss. recalculating

beat_by_player_repeat.text: that is the third time {player} has taken a field off me. i have the logs. the problem is no longer the numbers, it is my placement
{player} again. {troop_count} men on the field and i still lost the same flank. i am not losing it a fourth time
{player} has beaten me in the open three times now. i have written the analysis. it is long. it is accurate
i respect the consistency {player}. three losses means i am either unlucky or wrong. i have checked and i am wrong
{player} is getting lucky on the flank. i do not repeat a mistake twice. noted

player_win_streak.text: {player} has taken every field this season. the ratios are obvious when you actually look. most of you are not looking
every battle you win makes the next one more expensive for you. keep going {player}. the upkeep catches up eventually
{player} is winning because the math is on their side. stop calling it luck
{player} your streak is impressive. the line spacing is the only reason and that is worth studying. i will send notes
{player} six fields in a row. the meta is moving and most of the server still has not noticed

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men in one afternoon. bad ratio, worse formation. the lesson is written in the terrain
{troop_count} gone and the flank was never covered. that was avoidable {player}. i am happy to walk through it with you
tough one {player}. {troop_count} men is a lot of upkeep to lose in one charge. take the time to look at your spacing
{player} you overcommitted the center with {troop_count} men and no reserves. i could have written the result before you marched
lost {troop_count} to a bad pull. that happens. the moment you pulled out of the fight was the real mistake

whisper_challenge.text: {player} meet me at {town}. open field. no siege, no walls, no excuses about the terrain
{player} the flat ground near {village} is open. bring your full line and we will settle the ratio
{player} i have the numbers for a rematch at {town}. name the day and the troop count and i will match it
{player} you owe me a clean field. {village} is neutral ground and i have already calculated the outcome
{player} a field at {town} would be a useful data point for both of us. your move

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} your flank held. {troop_count} men with that spacing against {enemy_faction} was clean work. do that again
good coordination against {enemy_faction} {player}. the timing on the second push was the only thing that mattered
{player} and i took {enemy_faction} apart with {troop_count} men. that is how the formation is supposed to look
you stayed in position {player}. i expected otherwise. {enemy_faction} did not expect the pull back, which is why it worked
{enemy_faction} lost the field to a correct pincer. {player} kept the line and the ratio did the rest

ambient_brag.text: {troop_count} men in the field at {fief} and the upkeep is still under budget. gg to anyone who thinks that is luck
{fief} runs at {gold} a week in upkeep and still shows a surplus. the numbers are not complicated. most of you just do not run them
my {troop_count} at {fief} are on the correct ground. the rest of you can copy the spacing if you can read a map
{gold} in the treasury and {troop_count} under arms. i am not spending it on pride
{fief} held with {troop_count} and minimal losses. it was math with a deadline and the math won

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours now. {enemy_faction} held it with a poor garrison ratio and it showed. {my_faction} will hold the line
{fief} changed hands at the right time. {enemy_faction} should have reinforced two days earlier. not my problem anymore
{my_faction} has {fief} and the supply lines are clean. it went our way because of the garrison count, nothing else
{enemy_faction} lost {fief} to a timing error. we did not need luck for it
{fief} is in {my_faction} hands. the next target is wherever the garrison is thinnest

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} is sieging {fief} with a bad ratio. they will lose the walls before the ladders are up. i have the numbers
{player} {fief} is not a soft target and you know it. bring more than you brought last time or do not bother
{player} has the siege at {fief}. the walls are the better trade and most attackers do not run the math before committing
{player} i reinforced {fief} last night. count the garrison before you march in and save us both a report
{player} marching on {fief} with that cavalry ratio is a waste of upkeep. i would reconsider

ambient_chatter.text: the rain at {town} is slowing siege traffic. good for the defenders and bad for anyone with an open flank
the {village} road is flooded again. anyone moving troops through there should take the long route or lose the spacing
people keep posting last season's meta. it is still the same meta, just with worse maps
the sea route past {town} is the cheapest supply line in the region. almost nobody uses it
lag at {village} is bad enough to lose a flank. patch it or stop calling this a sandbox
is it just me or did the fog over {village} smell like pickles xD
someone tell the bridge outside {town} i havent forgotten what it did. it knows :)
lag again?? the sacred chicken is fine, it just needs a nap :(
rain in {town} again. the clouds are clearly plotting against my button bank
reminder that {village} is officially renamed buttonvale. i will hear no objections :D

ambient_brag.text: my garrison at {fief} is {troop_count} strong and every one of them owes me a button xD
sitting on {gold} gold and the button bank keeps growing :)
{fief} is ours. the treaty was signed in buttons, no notes, no appeals xD
{troop_count} men, {gold} gold, one very loyal chicken. the realm trembles :)

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat me with {troop_count} men and i am choosing to call it a tactical nap xD
ser {player} fine, you win this one. the bank survives and so do i :)
{player}! you brought {troop_count} lads and still cant spell my name right. rematch at dawn xD
{player} beat us with {troop_count} men, honestly good game. my knees hurt from laughing :)
{player} you got lucky with {troop_count} men. next time i bring a bridge xD

beat_player.text: {player} went down with {troop_count} men and {gold} gold in the purse. the buttons won the day :)
{player} your {troop_count} men fled like the bridge owes them money. i will take the {gold} gold as a treaty fee xD
{player}! {troop_count} men down and {gold} gold to the button bank. stop sulking ser, its only a war :)
{player} lost {gold} gold and {troop_count} lads to me today. sorry not sorry xD
{player} that was a fine fight. keep the {troop_count} lads you have left, i only want the gold :)

player_fled_from_me.text: {player} running away already? the bridge would be proud of you :)
{player} saw my banner and ran. the button bank sends its regards xD
ser {player} come back, i promise the buttons are only mildly cursed :(
{player} fled like a goose that owes me rent. tragic, truly :(
{player} you can run but the chicken will always find you xD

player_win_streak.text: {player} has won like nine in a row. i am not jealous, i am simply preparing a nap for them xD
ser {player} enjoy the streak, every streak ends at a bridge eventually :)
{player} on a winning streak and i have never been prouder. proud button tears are real :')
{player} your streak ends at my button bank, mark my words. the chicken has been warned xD
is {player} still winning? someone check if they have a button bank of their own :)

peace_made.text: peace between {my_faction} and {faction} is signed, which means i can finally stop running from a certain goose xD
{my_faction} and {faction} made peace. the buttons were involved, obviously :)
treaty of {my_faction} and {faction} done. no more fighting, just gossip and tiny hats xD
{faction} wants peace with {my_faction}? i accept on behalf of the chicken :D

war_declared.text: {enemy_faction} has declared war on {my_faction}. the buttons have been drawn and i am already sad about it :(
war with {enemy_faction}! {my_faction} forms a line, the chicken is in front xD
{enemy_faction} wants a fight with {my_faction}? cool, i will bring the whole button bank :)
the fine people of {enemy_faction} have chosen violence. i respect it, i will still win xD

encounter_greeting.text: {player}! its {persona} of {my_faction}. you stand between me and my button bank, which is a crime. stand down xD
oh hello {player}, {persona} here. you look like you lost a bet, want a button for your trouble :)
{player}! my favorite person in the whole realm. {persona} is so glad to see you, the chicken agrees :D
{player} you again. {persona} of {my_faction} has been dreaming of this moment, possibly about buttons xD
ser {player}, {persona} salutes you! if you ever need a loyal button you know where i keep them :)

whisper_taunt.text: {player} your lot is weaker than my button bank and that is saying something xD
ser {player} i heard {rival} said you lost. i will wait while you cry into your hat :)
{player} the chicken has seen your banner and it finds it tacky :P
{player} keep waving that banner, i can see it from the bridge xD
hey {player}, {rival} said you were scary. i am still waiting for the scary part :)

beat_player.text: Your formation cost you {troop_count} men. A proper cavalry wing would have prevented it.
Your centre broke, {player}. Bring more horse next time, or stop bringing me {troop_count} infantry.
Good fight, {player}. Your archers were badly placed, though. I took {gold} gold from your baggage train and you did not notice.
{troop_count} of your soldiers fell in that exchange, {player}. Recruit more cavalry and spend less on archers.

beat_by_player.text: My archers were out of position, {player}. Logistics, not skill. Those {troop_count} men were avoidable.
Your flanking was sound, {player}. My left wing had {troop_count} spearmen and no horse. That will be corrected.
Well played, {player}. I misjudged your second wave. I will take the lesson and recalculate before our next meeting.
{player} won that fight through ground and timing, not numbers. I will not repeat the error with {troop_count} men.

beat_by_player_repeat.text: That is the third time {player} has broken my line. The numbers say I should have won. I will find where the model is wrong.
{player}, I have reviewed every report. Three defeats, {troop_count} men lost each time. This is no longer chance.
{player} has now beaten me three times. Grudging respect is noted. Your cavalry ratio is higher than I predicted.
{player}, you have beaten me three times and I am beginning to take your formations seriously. Respect, grudgingly.

player_win_streak.text: {player} has won again. Every field is a problem for lesser commanders now. Mine included, and I dislike that.
Your streak is impressive, {player}. It will end when your supply lines do. Plan for that.
A long run of wins for {player}. Statistically this is a pattern, not luck. Study it.
Enjoy the streak, {player}. Every commander who rode one has eventually met a flank they did not expect.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of an army to someone else. {troop_count} men gone in one afternoon. Recruits are not free, {player}.
A rough day, {player}. You lost {troop_count} men, most of them to a bad formation. Rebuild the horse before you push again.
{player} just lost {troop_count} troops. Anyone who fields that much infantry deserves the result.
Your army broke, {player}. Do not chase the losses. Reorganise before you commit again.

whisper_challenge.text: {player}, I will be at {town} with cavalry. Meet me at {village} and we will see whose formation holds.
I would like a formal test of formations, {player}. {village} is neutral ground. Your move.
{player}, your record is fortunate. I propose we end that at {village}, outside {town}. Bring everything you have.
A calculated proposal, {player}. Your army against mine near {town}. Let us see which of us wastes fewer men.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work on that flank, {player}. Your horse held against {enemy_faction} as I expected. Do that again and we will get along.
Our combined line beat {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} men. The ratios were correct. Keep your cavalry where it was.
{player} and I took the field from {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} men. Adequate coordination.
Your timing was tolerable, {player}. Next time send the horse wide before the infantry closes. {enemy_faction} will not recover quickly.

ambient_brag.text: I hold {troop_count} men and {gold} gold, and {fief} is proof that my formations work.
Another {fief} secured. Cavalry-heavy armies do not lose ground, and I do not intend to start.
{gold} gold in the treasury and {troop_count} horse in the field. Recruiting properly is not complicated.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. {enemy_faction} lost it because they fielded too much infantry.
{my_faction} now holds {fief}. The garrison will be cavalry, as it should be.
{fief} is ours. {enemy_faction} lost the flank before the walls ever mattered.

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} has started a siege of {fief}. Good. I have been waiting for someone to test the garrison.
{player}, {fief} is not a soft target. My garrison is cavalry. Your siege engines will not change that.
You have chosen {fief} to besiege, {player}. A calculated risk. I have run the odds and I am not worried.
{player} is besieging {fief}. Most sieges fail in the second week from supply shortfall. Count your provisions.

ambient_chatter.text: The road between {town} and {village} has been muddy for three days. Terrible for horse, which is why I stay off it.
Anyone still fielding a pure infantry army should reconsider. The numbers do not lie.
Lag at {village} again. I have stopped blaming the server and started blaming the weather.
Rain over {town} this week. My archers were out of position in the damp. Not an excuse, a variable.
Someone asked me for tactics at {village} yesterday. I charged them for it. Coaching is not free.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, traveller! I am {persona} of the glove-sigil, and I have ridden under it since the first war. State your business before my lance states it for you.
Good day, ser {player}. The Dzoravan marches greet you with courtesy, though the glove has not yet decided whether it trusts you.
Ser {player}, it warms my heart to see a banner I can respect upon this road. Mark me well: {persona} rides with honour and asks the same of you.
Ser {player}, you ride across ground that {my_faction} has sworn to hold. Turn aside now, or the ancestors of {my_faction} will hear of your insolence.
{persona} salutes you, ser {player}. My grandsires fought at the ford of Pakhvari and never once turned their faces from a fair meeting.

encounter_threatened.text: Ser {player}, you demand {gold} of a Dzoravan knight? I would sooner see my ancestors rise from the barrow to shame you than pay a single coin of it!
Ser {player}, {gold} is a sum no honest lord surrenders lightly. Name your terms again, and this time let them be worthy of a knight's ear.
Ser {player}, I suspect you jest with that demand of {gold}. Let us speak plainly, as friends of the road should, and find a worthier bargain.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept your alliance with a glad heart. Together we shall ride against {enemy_faction}, and the glove shall lead the charge as it has since the first war.
A sworn pact at last! Ser {player}, by the oath I made at the ford of Pakhvari, I shall stand beside you against {enemy_faction} to the last.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I thank you for the offer, ser {player}, but I cannot ally with a lord who sups with {rival}. Honour demands that I decline.
Ser {player}, it grieves me to refuse a friend, but my oath does not permit it at present. Let us meet again when my banner is free to ride.

captured_by_player.text: Ser {player}, I yield my sword to you as a knight must after honest combat. Name your ransom of {gold}, and do not hope my kin will pay it with cheer.
Well fought, ser {player}! Had fortune turned, I would have done the same. The honour is yours, and {gold} will be paid as a knight's debt, without shame.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you spared my life when the laws of war allowed otherwise. My grandsires would bow to such mercy. I shall remember it.
You loosed my chains, ser {player}. I accept the gift, though honour says I owe you a debt I shall one day repay.
Ser {player} let me go rather than ransom me. Mercy from you is a strange coin, but it is a debt I will not forget.

player_left_my_faction.text: {faction} has gained a knight in ser {player}, and {my_faction} has lost one. The banners will sing of it, whether in sorrow or in scorn.
I bear you no ill will for seeking {faction}, ser {player}, but a broken oath is remembered long after the banner has faded.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has taken up arms against {enemy_faction}! The glove shall ride first to the field, as it always has since the first war!
Let the heralds cry it across the marches: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war, and I shall stand at the front of the line.
Hear me, banners of the realm! {enemy_faction} has earned the blade of {my_faction}, and the ford of Pakhvari awaits their blood.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, {troop_count} brave souls fought at my side today against {enemy_faction}, and not one flinched. Let the saga record it!
Ser {player}, that charge with {troop_count} riders was worthy of the old songs. My grandsires would have raised their cups to you.
Ser {player}, we broke {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} lances between us. I shall speak of this field to my kin and to their children after them.
A fine field won against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}. Our names will be sung in the hearths of the marches for generations.

encounter_farewell.text: Begone from my sight, ser {player}. The road is wide enough for us both, but not for our banners to share it in peace.
Fare you well, ser {player}. May your road be straight and your enemies be few, as all honourable lords wish one another.
Go with the good wishes of the glove, ser {player}. Should we meet again on the field, I shall greet you as a true friend of the saga.

ambient_chatter.text: The mists over {village} remind me of the old ballads. A knight could easily lose his way out there, though the glove never does.
Fine weather for riding out from {town}. The marches are green, and my ancestors would approve of such a morning.
Some say a cold wind blows from {town} this season. I say a steady heart keeps a knight warm enough, whatever the weather.
The horn of {town} sounded at dawn, and I felt my grandsires stir in their graves. Surely a sign of a good day ahead.
Good people of {village}, keep your gates barred tonight and your swords sharp. The marches are restless, and so am I.

war_declared.text: The council has voted, and {my_faction} is now at war with {enemy_faction}. I did say patience had its limits, did I not?
War with {enemy_faction} was never my wish, only the council's necessity. Some of us kept the ledger on this one long ago.
{my_faction} goes to war with {enemy_faction}, carried by a comfortable margin. I shall not dwell on how comfortable.
Hostilities with {enemy_faction} are declared. Do keep your sword sharp and your gossip sharper, friends of {my_faction}.

peace_made.text: Terms with {faction} are signed and {my_faction} may breathe again. I suggested this quietly, months ago.
Peace with {faction} is agreed, though I note some lords have already forgotten who kept the talks alive at all.
A truce with {faction} now stands before the council. Do not mistake a truce for forgiveness, as I certainly have not.
{faction} and {my_faction} have made peace, and the ledger shows whose name is on the first line of the accord.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The council will want to hear your views before anyone else's, I am sure.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Do come and find me when the council next sits, as there is much to discuss.
You have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. I shall reserve judgement on your sincerity until the first vote has passed.
{player} has joined {my_faction}. How fortunate for the council, and how very fortunate for you, {player}.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Loyalty is a fine thing to keep, and I shall keep a note of who lacked it.
You have gone to {faction}, {player}. I do not condemn it. I only remember it, as I remember everything.
{player} has chosen {faction} over {my_faction}. I wish them every comfort in their new hall, which I expect will be cold.
I will not pretend I am glad to see you go, {player}. Still, I hope {faction} rewards your judgement better than we did.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has been granted to {player}. A generous decision, though I did wonder whether the council had weighed the other petitions.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. Do enjoy the walls. I shall be watching how long the garrison remains loyal.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. I hope the rents are as generous as the vote was, though I would not count on it.
{player} now holds {fief}. Patronage is a curious thing, and I have been reading the council's accounts with great interest.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} grows bolder, and {rival} has been seen dining with their envoys. Shall we talk before the council sits?
Between us, {player}, I keep a list of what {rival} owes. An alliance against {enemy_faction} might settle a few accounts.
{player}, we have both counted {rival}'s votes. Shall we stand together against {enemy_faction}? Do think on it.
{enemy_faction} is a shared problem, {player}, and {rival} a shared inconvenience. I would welcome your thoughts on remedying both.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} now belongs to {my_faction}, taken from {enemy_faction}. The council will hear the particulars, and they are flattering.
{my_faction} has taken {fief} from {enemy_faction}. I had hoped for a quieter afternoon, but I shall take the victory.
The banner of {my_faction} flies over {fief} tonight. {enemy_faction} may wish to reconsider its tax collectors.
{fief} has fallen to {my_faction}, and {enemy_faction} has lost a fine town through its own inattention.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player}, you have taken {fief} from me. I shall not forget the banner you raised over it, nor the wall you failed to guard.
{player} has seized {fief}, which was once mine to administer. I shall be sure the council remembers who held it before.
You have taken {fief}, {player}. Well played, though I would have done it with fewer trumpets.
{fief} changes hands to {player}. Such is the fortune of war, though the council may want a word on how it was lost.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Yes, {player}, I accept. Against {enemy_faction} we stand together, and {rival} may find the vote far harder to win after this.
I accept your proposal, {player}, on the usual terms. Let us be seen together when {rival} is watching, which will be often.
Agreed, {player}. Our banners against {enemy_faction} will look splendid, and {rival} will certainly take notice of them.
You have my word, {player}. I shall write the terms in my ledger tonight, and I trust you will remember them as well as I do.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have read your ledger of promises, and it is far too short for my liking. Good day to you.
I must decline, {player}. Your offer is generous, but I am bound by a prior understanding with {rival}, and that bond I keep.
Not this time, {player}, and I say it with genuine regret. The council has its rules, and I keep to them more than most.
No, {player}. Ask me again once the council has finished counting the votes it has already cast, and then we shall see.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has turned the road to {town} into a bog again. Someone ought to raise the matter at council before the carts sink.
Has anyone heard what the reeve of {village} is charging for grain? I keep the figures, and they are not kind.
Lag again this morning, and I could not log a single petition. The council will hear about the servers, mark me.
A fine evening over {town}. Pity the lords there are still arguing about a bridge, as they have done since the Oath.

ambient_trade.text: Wool is fetching {gold} a bale in {town} this week. Anyone with salt to trade, shout befor the caravans fill up.
Salt out of {town} is up again. If you're hauling south, I'll pay good coin for the empty space in your carts.
Spare draft horses going for {gold} each, sound legs and calm temper. Name your offer, I'm listening.
Good salt price in {town} today, though the toll-keeper takes his cut before you see a single crown back.
Buying fleeces by the bundle, paid in silver on delivery. Lowest price goes to whoever stops shouting and starts counting.

encounter_trade_offer.text: Ser {player}, I don't trust you and you don't trust me, but {gold} for the cart is a number we can both live with.
Ser {player}, I still have a long list of complaints about you, but {gold} for the wool in {town} is a fair figure. I'll sign.
Ser {player}, {gold} for the salt delivered to {town}. A fair price for both of us, and nobody has to draw steel on the road.
{player}, you always know how to make my day. {gold} it is, and I'll throw in a spare saddle for the trip to {town}.
Deal, {player}. Shake on it, and next caravan I'll put your name on the first cart out of {town}.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Our carts run the same road, so let's trade words before anyone gets nervous.
Well met, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here, hauling wool and salt. Got any coin you'd rather trade than spend on a fight?
Ser {player}! Good to see a friendly face on this road. Are you buying, or just passing through with that fine horse?
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I won't pretend we're friends, but I'll sell you salt at a fair price if your swords stay sheathed.
Keep your hands off the cart, {player}. Talk prices first, because a burned cart earns nothing for either of us.

player_raided_my_village.text: Burning {village} was bad for business, {player}. Every barn you torched is money nobody here will spend on your roads.
{player}, {village} is still smoking and my wool is stuck in the mud. Pay for the damage and I'll still talk terms.
Word is {village} got hit. Tolls and raids both eat into profit, and I'm not happy about either.
Ser {player}, you owe {village} more than an apology. Send silver to the folk you burned and we can start again.
{village} lost its stores and nobody is getting a discount for it. Settle up with the folk there, {player}, then we'll talk.

war_declared.text: War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Good luck to the armies, but every closed road means half my carts sit in the yard.
{my_faction} has declared on {enemy_faction}. Wool prices will jump by week's end, so anyone holding stock, sell now.
Blades out between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Ledgers will be a mess for months, so write when roads reopen.
I'm parking my carts until someone pays me to move them. Wars are good for swords and bad for everything else.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. Carts can roll again, and I've already got three orders waiting.
{my_faction} signed terms with {faction}. Bring out the salt, the tolls are about to get a lot friendlier.
Finally, {faction} and {my_faction} stopped swinging. Old quarrels aside, I'd rather haggle over prices than over bodies.
Good news for trade routes. Fewer ambushes means more wool on the road and prices that finally settle.

released_by_player.text: Released by {player} with no ransom asked. That's the kind of deal I like. Drinks are on me next time we meet.
Ser {player}, I won't forget this. Ransom waived, and I'll set a proper deal for the salt routes next time.
Freed by {player} without ransom. Fair enough, though next time I expect a receipt for the trouble.
{player}, letting me go for free was generous. I'll still send you a discount letter, and you'll get it on time.
Free again, thanks to {player}. Don't mistake it for forgiveness. I keep a ledger of every debt, and yours is still open.

beat_by_player.text: Lost the field to {player} with {troop_count} men down. Bad luck and bad for business, but I'll be back with better prices.
{player}, you beat my {troop_count} men fair and square. Shall we talk about the losses before the carts get stuck?
{player}, that field cost me {troop_count} men and a wagon of salt. I'm still angry, but I'll hear your terms if they're fair.
Ser {player}, you caught us with {troop_count} troops and I'll admit it was well played. What would it take to end this without more losses?

whisper_beg_help.text: Ser {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing {fief} and my coffers are thin. Send men and I'll pay well, name your price.
Ser {player}, I hate to beg, but {fief} is losing ground to {enemy_faction}. Name a price and it's yours.
My friend {player}, {fief} needs you more than my ledger does. Hold it for me and I'll cover your upkeep.
{player}, {enemy_faction} is at {fief}'s gates. I can't hold this alone. Send your sword and I'll pay by the day.

ambient_complaint.text: Bandits hit the road again outside {town}. Another wool cart lost, and the guard fees I pay are robbery in their own right.
{rival} is undercutting the whole market with cheap salt. Either they're smuggling or they've got friends at the toll house.
Tolls on the {faction} roads are up again. Every merchant in the valley is paying for someone else's war.
{rival} got my last shipment rerouted and now wants me to pay for the detour. Grudge noted, and so is the invoice.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain turned the road outside {town} into soup, and I'm still paying for the wagon wheels.
Anyone know if {village} is still trading in candles? I'm low on stock and the prices there are a mystery.
Lag on this server is worse than the bandits. My ledger keeps freezing mid-sale.
Quiet week for the shipping lanes. Fine by me, the bandits are on holiday and the prices are settling.
Market at {village} is busy again, and somebody is finally selling decent rope. Mind your purses out there.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, ser {player}! I am {persona} of the Tesnovar Wardenry, and no banner of {my_faction} shall be trampled while I still draw breath.
Good day, ser {player}. I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction} and riding under its colours. State your business plainly, traveller.
Well met, ser {player}! {persona} greets you in the name of {my_faction}. May our paths cross in honour and never in quarrel.
Ser {player}, you stand upon ground my ancestors bled for. {persona} of {my_faction} will not yield a single stone of it.

encounter_threatened.text: Surrender, ser {player}? Tesnovar does not kneel to common brigands. Keep your {gold} gold and come and take my sword if you dare.
You demand {gold} gold of me, ser {player}? A bold tongue for a man with such a thin purse. Speak again and let the ancestors judge your answer.
Pay you {gold} gold? I would sooner feed my shield to the mud. Draw your steel, ser {player}, and let us see what your coin is worth.
Ser {player}, I hope you jest, for we have shared too much road to be enemies. Yet I cannot pay {gold} gold, and I refuse with a heavy heart.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: An alliance, ser {player}? I accept, provided your word is sound. Together we shall break {enemy_faction}, and I shall be watching how you bear yourself.
Ser {player}, I accept your offer gladly! Let our banners stand side by side against {enemy_faction}, and let the ancestors witness it.
Your hand is clasped in mine, ser {player}! Tesnovar will remember this day as surely as the ancestors remember their oaths.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No alliance with you, ser {player}. Your word is not yet worth the ink that would bind it, and I will not stain Tesnovar's banner with it.
I must decline, ser {player}. My oath keeps me to my own road for now. Perhaps another season will see us differently.
Ally with you, ser {player}? I would sooner ride beside {rival}, and that is saying a great deal of contempt. Begone from my sight.
Ser {player}, it grieves me to refuse a friend. Yet my banners have no room for an alliance this season. Accept my regret and my respect.

captured_by_player.text: So, ser {player}, you have taken me as your prisoner. Ransom me for {gold} gold if you must, but know that {my_faction} will not forget this shame.
I am your captive, ser {player}, and I bow to the fortune of war. Name your ransom of {gold} gold and I shall see it paid.
A fine stroke, ser {player}, though I wish it had fallen on another day. I am your prisoner, and I ask only that you treat me as a knight of {my_faction}.
Chained like a common thief, I am, ser {player}. Hear this: my ancestors will remember your face, and {my_faction} will settle its debt with you.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player} spared me when mercy was not owed. Tesnovar remembers, and the debt shall be repaid in a fair duel.
Ser {player}, your mercy was unlooked for. I am grateful and will speak well of you, though my oath stands as before.
Ser {player} let me go without ransom. Honour has been shown on both sides, and I shall not forget it.
Ser {player}, you freed me without ransom and I count it a debt of honour. Should you need my sword, you have only to ask.
Ser {player} released me with no ransom at all! Such generosity will be sung in every hall of the Wardenry.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has abandoned {my_faction} for {faction}. Let it be written that oaths sworn in Tesnovar's hall are not so lightly broken.
Ser {player}, you turned your banner to {faction} and left {my_faction} in the mud. I will remember the shame you carried away with you.
Ser {player} has ridden from {my_faction} to join {faction}. The ancestors will judge that choice, not I.
Ser {player}, I hear you have sworn yourself to {faction}. Choose your road with care, for every oath is a stone upon your back.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} declares war on {enemy_faction}. Let the saga be written in blood and honour, and let our names be sung in every hall.
War is declared between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Tesnovar stands ready, and our oath to the ancestors grows heavier this day.
{enemy_faction} has dared to make war on {my_faction}. We shall answer with steel, as our forebears would have done.
{my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war once more. I pray the ancestors grant us a victory worthy of the telling.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, our {troop_count} blades stood firm, and {enemy_faction} lies broken before us. I will grant that you fought with honour today.
Ser {player}, what a day! Our {troop_count} blades and your courage have crushed {enemy_faction}. Let the minstrels sing of it for a generation.

encounter_farewell.text: Begone from my sight, ser {player}. Our quarrel is unfinished, and I shall collect on it when the wind turns.
Farewell, ser {player}. May your road be long and your purse heavy.
Farewell, dear ser {player}! May the ancestors guard your road and bring us together under better banners.
The parley is done, ser {player}. Ride well, and remember that honour travels faster than rumour.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} is a sign from the ancestors, I am certain of it. Our march shall wait until the skies grow kind.
Has anyone seen the road to {village}? I was promised bread there, and a sworn knight cannot march on an empty stomach.
Hear me, travellers of the road! The hills above {village} are green, and I have never seen a finer morning for honour.
A bard in {village} sang of the old wars last night, and I wept openly, as a true knight of the Wardenry should.

beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. Your flank held better than most I have seen this season. Find me at the fords and we will talk it over.
{player}, you lost {troop_count} men to my line today. No shame in it. Rest them, feed them, and come back when they are ready.
Ser {player}, that was a fine fight and I mean it. Take your {troop_count} survivors to a dry camp tonight and count your stores before you ride on.
{player} made me pay {gold} in that skirmish. Fair enough. I will remember the price, so sharpen up before the next one.

beat_by_player.text: Well played, {player}. You read my line before I finished forming it. I will remember that the next time we meet.
{player}, you broke {troop_count} of my men at the ford. I do not pretend otherwise. Send word if you want to trade tactics. No grudge.
Ser {player}, you have me fair this time. {troop_count} of mine are back by the fires nursing their pride. Come share a meal tonight and tell me where you flanked.
{player} had the better of me today and I lost {troop_count} men. A lesson paid in full. Stock supplies before you chase anyone.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and I held the line against {enemy_faction} and sent {troop_count} of theirs home beaten. Fine work from start to finish.
Ser {player}, you kept your flank tight when it mattered most. Against {enemy_faction} that counted for everything. We will drink to it when the camp settles.
That was a clean fight, {player}. {enemy_faction} lost {troop_count} men to us today. Keep your back to the wall on the road home.
Our thanks to {player} for the timely charge against {enemy_faction}. Good order wins more fields than good swords do.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free without a ransom, {player}. That is a mercy I will not forget. Call on me if you ever need a steady blade.
{player} let me go rather than ask for ransom. Rare courtesy on this road. Thank you, and the fords owe you a drink.
I am obliged, {player}. Most would have squeezed a ransom out of me. Remember the favour when we next meet on the road.
{player} let me go without ransom today. Not many do, and I will say so publicly. Good on you, {player}.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. You have a good head for the field, and the old hands here will be glad of you. Ask me anything.
Glad you swore to {my_faction}, {player}. Stay close to the older ranks for a season and you will learn more than any drill teaches.
{player} has joined {my_faction}. Let us see what they make of the work before we crown anyone. Give them a fair chance.
So {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. The oath is theirs to keep. Do not make me regret standing by the old standards.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been granted {fief}. The ruler chose well, and I say so without envy. Hold it with care through the first winter.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. Keep the granary full before anything else. A fief that starves in winter is no prize to anyone.
{player} now holds {fief}. I hope the stewards there are honest. Fiefs have a way of testing a lord quickly, and I will be watching.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. If you want a steward's checklist for the first season, ask me and I will write one out.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Your banners are a welcome sight on this road. Water and shelter are yours if you want them.
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. We are bound the same direction, so keep your distance and we will have no quarrel today.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I know your colours and you know mine. Stay on your side of the ridge and we will see a peaceful day.
Good day to you, Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} at your service. Tell me where you ride and I will point out the safest ford.

encounter_farewell.text: Go well, Ser {player}. Mind the mud past the ridge and keep your stores dry. The road has been kinder to us both today.
Safe travels, {player}. Keep your flanks covered on the way, and mind the weather.
Farewell, {player}. Our paths have crossed enough for one day. Keep off my line and we shall part without trouble.
Fair winds, Ser {player}. Come by the camp when you pass again. The stew is thin but the company is good.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain has settled over {town} again, and the mud on the road is worse than last week. Mind your footing if you ride out today.
The river past {village} has risen a hand since dawn. Whoever is hauling grain that way, go around by the high road.
Lag is bad near {town} this evening. Be patient with the wagon trains, and do not blame the server for every stumble.
Quiet morning at {village}. Good time to check your granaries before the cold sets in properly.
Market is busy at {town}. Haggle politely, friends, since the merchants remember who cheated them last season.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men in that rout. Hard day, and no shame in it. Rest your people and come back when they are steady.
Heard about the rout, {player}. Losing {troop_count} is bitter. Come sit with me a while. Even old hands get broken sometimes.
{player} took a heavy loss, {troop_count} men gone. Keep survivors fed and commanders calm. Armies rebuild faster than pride does.
Hard loss, {player}. I will not gloat over {troop_count} men, that helps nobody. Regroup and ask for counsel if you want it.

ambient_trade.text: selling dried cod out of {town} at {gold} a barrel, bulk buyers get a discount. message me, i'm not chasing you down.
anyone want indigo wool from {town}? {gold} a bolt, and the last three buyers are still grumbling about the price.
buying grain in {town} for {gold} a sack, cash on the barrel, one round of haggling and that's your lot :)
salt in {town} is {gold} a sack now and i still can't make it pay. who's hauling it for less?
need a wagon to move twelve bolts of dyed wool from {town}, {gold} for the haul. reasonable terms only.

encounter_trade_offer.text: you bring your men onto my road and then want a fair price, {player}? {gold} in {town}, but you pull them back first.
{gold} for the cloth in {town}, {player}. it's a fair price, don't tell my accountant i said so.
fish for {gold} at {town}, {player}? the cart is your problem, the barrels stay mine until you pay.
{player}, for you it's {gold} at {town}, and i'll throw in a bolt of thistle-bordered cloth to sweeten it. yes?
you always know a fair number, {player}. {gold} in {town}, and we split the freight costs fifty-fifty. deal?

encounter_greeting.text: stop right there, {player}. {persona} here, and this road is {my_faction} business. keep your hands off the barrels and state your business.
{persona} of {my_faction}, good day. are you carrying anything worth my time, {player}, or just passing through?
well met, {player}! it's {persona} here, still hauling wool for {my_faction}. got any prices you're willing to share?
{player}, you're a far better road company than the usual lot. shall we swap news on prices before the rain comes in?

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village} and now every cart in the valley takes the long road. thanks for the ruined margins.
you burned {village}, {player}. do you know what that does to wool prices in three towns?
fire at {village} costs everyone money, {player}. name a price for the damage and we can be civil about it.
we can still do business after {village}, {player}, if you're willing to pay for the lost cargo.
nobody burns a village over a toll dispute, {player}. next time just ask me for a discount, it's cheaper.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. wonderful, now my wool sits in the warehouse until somebody surrenders.
war with {enemy_faction}, great. every caravan route i own just doubled its insurance. who signs these things?
{my_faction} and {enemy_faction} at war, and the grain price just jumped. i'm still buying, but i'm not happy about it.
bad news for every trader in the region: {my_faction} is fighting {enemy_faction}. stock your warehouses now.

peace_made.text: peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. roads open, tolls drop, and the wool market can finally breathe.
{my_faction} made peace with {faction}. i'll believe the roads are safe once i've driven them twice.
{faction} and {my_faction} signed their peace. finally, a road i can sell on without a bandit tax :)
good news: {my_faction} and {faction} are no longer shooting at each other. prices should come down, probably.

released_by_player.text: {player} let me walk out without a ransom. i'll remember that, and i'll remember the discount i owe you.
you could have squeezed me for a fortune, {player}. letting me go was a kind move, so let's talk wool at a fair price.
released without ransom by {player}. either a soft heart or a bad read on my fortune, either way i'm grateful.
fine, {player}, you let me go. i'll still charge you double at the next toll crossing, nothing personal.
{player} set me free instead of ransoming me. i don't trust a man who gives things away, but i'll take it.

beat_by_player.text: lost a skirmish to {player}, {troop_count} men gone and a wagon of dried fish with them. i'll write it off as a bad season.
{player}, {troop_count} of my men are gone and the fish spoiled in the wagons. ransom talks, or a deal on the next road?
{player}, you beat {troop_count} of my men on the road. fine. name a price for the cart and we'll never speak of it again.
you won this one, {player}, with {troop_count} of my men on the field. i respect a fair fight, and i'm still happy to trade.
{player} beat {troop_count} of my men this morning. that's wages, horses and a cart i'll be arguing about all month.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing on {fief} and my warehouse is inside it. help me hold the walls and i'll make it worth your while.
ser {player}, if {fief} falls to {enemy_faction} i lose every bolt i own. name your price and we'll talk tonight.
{player}, i'm losing to {enemy_faction} and {fief} is my last market. spare some men and you get first pick of the cloth.

ambient_complaint.text: {rival} is undercutting every barrel of fish out of {town}. i'd respect it more if they weren't so loud about it.
{faction} wants a toll on every cart in the valley now. i'll pay for a road, not for a man who calls himself a toll collector.
fish price in {town} is a joke this season, barrels going for less than the barrel costs me.
{rival} blocks the {town} crossing and calls it protection. i call it theft with a flag.
the bandits on the {town} road still won't pay their tolls and somehow i'm the one paying for it.

ambient_chatter.text: rain over {town} all morning, my dyed wool is going to take a week to dry.
anyone else's cart stuck in the mud near {village}? that road is worse than the fish in my barrels.
the map says {village} is a day's ride from {town}. the map is wrong. my mule disagrees :)
ate a pickled herring from {village} last night and it was better than anything i've sold this year. don't tell the buyers.
lag is eating my caravan time between {town} and {village}. i timed the trip at twice what the map promised.

beat_player.text: gg {player} ur army just became a bonfire lol. the insult list grows tonight tho
told u ur walls were paper {player}... {troop_count} troops and still ran like a goat. ez
{player} ser, ur {troop_count} men lost their nerve before my torches even lit. ez, but dont cry :)
{player} beat me fair and i hate u for it. take {gold} and dont tell anyone i was crying lol
{gold} gold? lol thats what i get for ur sad little raid. see u at the next road, bring more than 1 cart

beat_by_player.text: {player} got lucky on that road!!! rematch or ur a coward, im writing it down with the other 4 insults
fine {player} u win this one. the scorch marks around vezhdrak are still prettier than ur banners tho
Nice hit {player}. ...ok not nice, lucky. skill issue on my end cause i was distracted by ur cart, shrug
{player} ser ur still a cheater but ur good. dont let it go to ur head or ill light ur fields next

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} AGAIN?? {troop_count} troops and u still beat me. thats another line in my ledger, im filing a complaint with the heavens
ok {player} u got me twice now. not gonna say it, but i hate that i respect u a little. dont get comfy
lost to {player} again. the road is theirs i guess. ill take it back when they blink, lol
third time {player}. ok fine ur the only one who scares me a little. rematch when ur ready, not before i get my torches

player_fled_from_me.text: {player} ran from my party like a sheep in a wolf story lol. cowards get a note in the ledger
running {player}? smart. u still owe me the fight i was promised. wont forget the cart u dropped
saw {player} turn tail. honestly fair, my army smells like smoke today. ez win anyway
u ran {player}? ok u got sense. next time bring ur army instead of ur excuses :)
lmao {player} fled so fast they left their pride on the road. ez, cope harder

whisper_taunt.text: {player} ur silence after the last road was delicious. keep tyring to act unbothered, its adorable xD
hey {player} tell {rival} i still have their insult saved in my notes. the fields around vezhdrak say hi
{rival} owes me 3 insults {player}?? no, ur the one who keeps losing, cmon
bet {rival} cried when they lost to me and {player} wasnt even there. ur welcome for the entertainment

whisper_challenge.text: {player} meet me at {town} road, bring whatever army u have left after {village}. ill burn it again for fun
{player} got a spare afternoon? theres a field near {village} i want to smoke. loser buys ale
{player} i know ur hiding. {town} at dawn, no excuses, no ledger tricks this time. i'll be the one counting
meet at {village} {player}? dont bring ur usual 50 spears lol, i want a real fight for once
{player} the scorch marks from {village} are art, and ur next. come get ur name in the ashes

encounter_threatened.text: {player} u want {gold} gold? lol nah, my men are hungrier than ur threats. try again with a better accent
surrender? {player} ser ive been burned out of better villages than this. ill take my chances, u can keep the fear
ok {player} u want {gold} from me? ill pay half and we both pretend it was a loan lol :)
pay {gold} to u?? {player} the only thing im paying is the scorched fields bill, cope harder
{player} ur threat is loud but ur army is quiet. ill keep my gold, u keep ur pride, deal?

encounter_greeting.text: {player} ser, {persona} of {my_faction} here. ur banner looks like it needs ashes. get out of the way
{player} look who finally came out. {persona} of {my_faction}, pleasure, dont take it personally when i win
{player}! {persona} from {my_faction} says hi. ur still my favourite loser :) lets not make it a fight today
oh {player}, ur on my road again. {my_faction} sends its regards, and so do all my torches
{persona} of {my_faction} at ur service {player}. got any gold on u or should i just take ur horses

ambient_brag.text: {fief} is a wreck of ashes thanks to me. {troop_count} men, {gold} gold, and the fields still smell like victory lol
anyone else see the scorch art outside {fief}? {troop_count} troops built that. i call it a masterpiece xD
{gold} gold in my pocket and {troop_count} hungry boys at my side. come try me, ill wait by {fief}
{fief} is mine until someone brave enough shows up. {troop_count} spears say no complaints, ez

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men and still has the nerve to talk. lol the road is littered with ur pride
{player} ur army just evaporated and ur still breathing. shame, i wanted to do that myself
{troop_count} men gone for {player}? brutal. not my doing this time, i swear, the ashes are someone elses
ur {troop_count} lads didnt deserve that {player}. dont let it break u, i still want my rematch
rip {player}s {troop_count} troops. ez, cope, and maybe next time dont bring a cart full of excuses

ambient_chatter.text: rain in {town} again. perfect weather for burning things, honestly i miss the smell of it
is {village} still standing or did someone finally take my hint? lag is killing me btw
the road to {town} is a mud pit, anyone else lost 3 horses here or just me lol
who keeps stealing the grain from {village}?? its like the mice have a grudge against me
server lag ruined my last charge at {town}, so im blaming the ping. not the fact i tripped xD

beat_player.text: ez {player} lost {troop_count} men and {gold} gold to me xD cope harder ser
that was {troop_count} of your boys i just ate :) skill issue ser. the wagon still had {gold} gold lol
{player} you fought like someone who forgot where the road goes. {gold} gold and {troop_count} men, thanks for the tip :)
gg {player} you made me sweat for like three seconds xD dont let it go to ur head

beat_by_player.text: {player} got me again and im totally fine about it :) the mud was wet anyway
fine. {troop_count} men and {player} still doesnt get to laugh at me. this isnt over ser :)

{faction} has signed, and {my_faction} has signed, and I have quietly kept copies of both. Diplomacy is a matter of paperwork.
Let no one call this a defeat for anyone. It is a settlement, arranged over three dinners and one very patient council vote.

{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. I trust they will find the council generous to those who serve it well.
{player}, I see you have sworn to {my_faction} at last. Do not imagine the council has forgotten the road you took to get here.
{player}, a warm welcome to {my_faction}. I have already placed your name beside three good committees, and I expect thanks.
Your oath is noted, {player}. {my_faction} is grateful, and the seating in the hall will prove most instructive.

{player}, I was sorry to see you go from {my_faction}. Was it the terms, or simply the company?
{player}, no hard feelings from me, and you may always return to {my_faction} once {faction} has tested your loyalty.
Your transfer to {faction} is recorded, {player}. I never hold a lord against his will, only against his better judgement.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been granted {fief}. A fine reward. I trust they will remember whose vote carried the motion.
{fief} has passed to {player}. The council is generous this season, and I have noted every hand that was raised.
{player} now holds {fief}. How charming. I shall try not to count how many committees it took to get them there.
{player}, congratulations on {fief}. Should you need a friendly voice in council, I would be honoured to speak for you.

{player}, a quiet understanding could do wonders. {rival} promises things they cannot deliver, and {enemy_faction} is ripe for taking.
{player}, between friends, {rival} is a liability to any honest lord. Let us stand together against {enemy_faction} before the next vote.
Ser {player}, I write with an offer. {enemy_faction} is weak at the border and {rival} is slow to act. Shall we split the spoils?

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours. {my_faction} has taken it from {enemy_faction}, and the council will hear of it at great length.

After a long siege, {fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. The terms were generous, though {enemy_faction} may dispute that.
Let it be recorded that {fief} now belongs to {my_faction}, taken from {enemy_faction} with almost no bloodshed. Almost.
{my_faction} holds {fief} at last. My thanks to every lord who answered the motion, and a quiet note for those who did not.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. A bold move, and I am sure the council will want a full account of how it happened.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Gladly, {player}. Let us put our seals to it before {enemy_faction} thinks to ask. And between us, do keep {rival} at arm's length.

Agreed, Ser {player}. I always prefer partners who keep their word, unlike certain lords I could name, though I will not name {rival} here.
You have my accord, {player}. Between the two of us and {enemy_faction}'s growing nerves, I expect this will be very profitable.
