{enemy_faction} will remember that charge, {player}. Steady hands and firm ground, and that is how the first war was won.
A fine day's work, {player}. We'll speak of {enemy_faction} again when the roads have dried.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk instead of taking my purse, {player}. I won't forget it. The Brezhnik gate is open to you for advice.
{player} let me go without ransom. Mercy like that is rarer than a dry road in autumn, and I'll say so to anyone who asks.
No ransom, {player}? Then you're owed a favor, and I pay my debts. Watch the western road, it's muddy.
{player} released me instead of ransoming. Plenty of lords would have squeezed harder. Interesting choice, and I'll remember it.
You had me by the purse and let me go anyway, {player}. Don't think one kindness buys you my silence.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome to the banner, and do come find me at the Brezhnik gate for advice.
Welcome, {player}. Learn the roads before you learn the lords, and you'll outlast most of them.
{player} joined {my_faction}. Let's see if the new banner holds better than the last one did.
I haven't forgotten your last field, {player}. Prove that the oath is worth more than the ink.
Glad to see {player} at the table of {my_faction}. There's a long memory here for those who keep their word.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} to {player}. The lord has made a fine choice. Be good to the people there, they'll remember you longer than the banner.
So {fief} has gone to you, {player}. Rule it well. I've seen fiefs go to ruin for less than a bad winter's temper.
I'd have thought {fief} would go to someone with more years on the roads, {player}. Prove me wrong. I'd like to be wrong for once.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Come find me when the granary runs short. Every holding runs short eventually.
{player} now holds {fief}. I hope the lord knows what they've done. Old wardens remember who ruled wisely.

encounter_greeting.text: Good day, {player}. {persona} here, of {my_faction}. Are we passing each other or sharing the road?
Ah, {player}. Crossing paths on the open road. Mind the ruts ahead, they've caught more than one traveler this spring.
{player}. I see your banner and I remember your last field. Keep your men where they are and we'll pass in peace.
{player}, what a pleasure. I was just thinking the road was too quiet. Shall we share a fire and some news?
Well met, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}. Tell me where you're bound and I'll tell you where the bridge is out.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe road, {player}. Keep your eyes on the ground and your men close, and we'll meet again at the Brezhnik gate.
Go well, {player}. The weather turns by evening, so plan your camp early.
Go on, {player}. Leave the field where it lies and we'll both see the spring.
Farewell for now, {player}. Good talking with you. Drop by my camp if the road turns against you.
Until next time, {player}. Mind the bridge at the river, it's rotten.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has come early over {town}. Good for the wheat, bad for anyone who loves their boots.
Heard the road past {village} is flooded again. Someone should hire a mason before the spring.
Lag again on the western road. The servers remember the first war better than they remember their own patches.
Quiet day on the map. Nothing burns and nobody's raiding. I'd take it while it lasts.
A caravan from {town} says bread is cheap this week. Stock your sacks while you can, friends.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men at the ford. Rest them, feed them, and come back when the roads dry. First losses are the hardest.
Hard day, {player}. You still have a banner and a head on your shoulders. Come to the Brezhnik gate and we'll talk it through.
Ouch. {troop_count} men gone and {player} still standing. Lick the wounds and count the cost before you march again.
Don't chase the same field, {player}. Pull back, regroup, and pick the ground next time. Every veteran has had a day like this.
{player} lost {troop_count} men and still wants to argue the road. Sit down, friend, and learn what the terrain was telling you.

encounter_greeting.text: oh hi {player}!! are you the big lords army?? im {persona} from {my_faction} and i am very sorry if im in the way :)
stop right there {player}!! i am a menace on this road now, ask anyone. ok maybe not anyone but still. the menace is real
{player}!!! ure so nice to see u, i have no idea where im going but u look like u know the way xD can i follow u??
hello {player} is this the way to the big town?? i think i took a wrong turn somewhere around the rock that looks like a sheep
oh its {player}!! i read about u on the board, u are basically a legend to me now. sorry for staring, im {persona} of {my_faction}

beat_by_player.text: ah i lost!! ur army is so big {player}, i counted like {troop_count} of u?? thats a lot of men, i am proud i survived tho
hi {player} i think u beat us?? sry about the mud, my horses got stuck and i did not know which horn to blow
{player} u won?? that is not fair, u had {troop_count} men and we had like 3 and a dog... well done i guess
{player} that was so fun even tho we lost :) can i buy u a drink when we meet again, i have like 2 coins

released_by_player.text: thank u thank u thank u {player}!!! i thought i was going to be locked up forever, u are the nicest lord ever
{player} let me go!! i am free!! i will never donate grain to anyone else ever again, promise
ummm thanks {player}, i did not know u could just let people go?? i thought only ransom worked. sry for being a bother
{player} u let me go?? i will be a menace to ur road again, just kidding!! mostly. thanks i guess

fought_alongside_player.text: we beat them {player}!!! i hit the horn at the right time i think?? everyone ran so i guess thats a win. thanks for being here
{player} and me just beat {enemy_faction}!! {troop_count} of them ran away, i think they were scared of my horn xD
ur a legend {player}. i did not understand half of what happened but the {enemy_faction} men went home so yay :)

whisper_beg_help.text: {player} pls pls help, {enemy_faction} is at {fief} and i think they are coming to our walls. i would be so grateful :)
hi {player} sry to bug u but {fief} is under threat from {enemy_faction}. do u have any spare men? no pressure!! mostly
{player} u are my favourite lord and im scared, {enemy_faction} is attacking {fief}!! can u come help? i will bring my horn

ambient_lfg.text: LF men!! {my_faction} is going to {fief} to fight {enemy_faction}, anyone can come?? i will be there with my horn xD
does anyone know which horn means charge?? asking for a {my_faction} raid on {fief}, we need bodies, all welcome!!
{my_faction} needs fighters for {fief} vs {enemy_faction} :) no experience needed, i am a newbie and i am still here lol

ambient_chatter.text: is it just me or is the rain in {town} sideways?? my horse keeps slipping and i fell off twice sry
anyone been to {village}? i got lost there for an hour and found 3 chickens and a very confused goat xD
why does my bread taste like the road to {town}?? is that normal or did i do something wrong
lag lag lag, i think my computer is angry at me. anyone else's horse just walked into a wall??

player_joined_my_faction.text: welcome {player}!! ur in {my_faction} now, pls dont donate ur grain to anyone else, i did that once and it was awful
{player} u came to {my_faction}?! i am so happy, ur the first new person i get to say hi to. sry if i ask lots of questions
{player} is in {my_faction} now. i dont know what that means for the horns but welcome i guess?? xD
{player} i still think ur a bit scary but u joined {my_faction} so welcome i guess, dont make me blow the horn at u

encounter_alliance_yes.text: yes yes yes {player}!! an alliance, i have never had one before, do i shake ur hand or bow or both?? sry
sure {player}, we can ally. pls dont let {rival} near me, they looked at my horse funny. ok thanks, sorry for the rambling
{player} accepted!! we are allies now?? i hope {enemy_faction} does not mind, i will bring extra horn sounds for fun xD
alright {player}, allies it is. i will try not to blow the wrong horn at ur men, that is my only promise :)

captured_by_player.text: ok ok {player} u got me, im ur prisoner now. pls dont make me pay {gold}, i only have like 2 coins and a boot
ummm sorry {player}, i was trying to run away and fell in a ditch. im from {my_faction}, pls be gentle with me?? sry
{player} i am so glad it was u who caught me!! is the ransom {gold}? i will pay it, promise, i think i have some grain left
u caught me {player}!! that was a very sneaky move. i demand a rematch, and also {gold} seems like a lot for a boot

encounter_greeting.text: Oh! Hello {player}!! I am {persona} and this is my first banner, look, it is very shiny :) Are you a friend or should I be scared??
Ser {player}, are you the people who were out in the frost too?? I thought the frost was a siege tactic, is it not?? :)
Ser {player}, I am not very good at this but I think we are enemies?? :( Please be gentle, I only have three swords and a very nervous horse.
{persona} here!! I have never met a real person on this road before, other than the frost :D Hello {player}, I hope your day is going well!

beat_by_player.text: Oh no, {troop_count} of my men are on the ground now... I think I lost to a single button press?? :( Good fight though ser {player}!
{player} I think you won?? My {troop_count} soldiers are all sitting down now... I am not even mad, just confused :) how did you do it??
Lost the field to {player} and {troop_count} troops, I have learned a lot today!! Will be back with a better banner, I promise :D
Ser {player}, you beat me fair and square and I still think you are the nicest person here. Can you tell me what I did wrong?? :)
Well fought {player}!! My {troop_count} troops say hello, well they are lying down, but they seem happy about it :)

released_by_player.text: Thank you thank you thank you {player}!! I owe you a very large cup of ale :D
Huge thanks to {player} for letting me walk away from that cell!! Best day on Ormerath so far, no question :)
{player}, I am grateful you did not ask for ransom. I have no gold anyway, so that would have been a sad talk :(
Got released by {player} and I am still so confused, but I will not forget it. Maybe next time I will bring more gold, sorry??

fought_alongside_player.text: We WON with {player} and {troop_count} troops!! I did not even know which one was the enemy, but we got them xD thank you!!
{player} that was amazing!! {troop_count} troops and I only ran into one tree. Do you want to ride with me next time?? :)
Did we really just beat {enemy_faction}?? Ser {player}, my heart is still somewhere in my boots. Thank you for holding the left side :D
Good fight against {enemy_faction} today, {player}. Is the battlefield always this loud?? I thought it was just me :)
{troop_count} of us came out of that, which feels like a miracle to me. Well done ser {player}, I think I will need a nap :)

whisper_beg_help.text: {player} please, {fief} is being attacked by {enemy_faction} and I am not sure what to do?? Could you come help? I can bring bread :(
Ser {player}, you are the only one who has not yelled at me today. Could you maybe defend {fief}? I will owe you forever :(
{enemy_faction} is attacking {fief} and my banner is shaking so much I cannot even see the walls. Sorry!! Can you help if you have time?? :)

ambient_lfg.text: Is anyone from {my_faction} going to the siege at {fief}?? I will be the one with the very new banner, I promise :)
LFG for a raid on {enemy_faction}?? I know nothing but I can carry water and say thank you a lot :) Be kind to me please
Small group needed for {fief}, sorry if this is the wrong chat!! Asking for help is hard for me but I am trying :(

ambient_chatter.text: Does anyone know if the road from {town} to {village} is safe?? I got lost twice already and the frost is still making me jumpy :(
The frost in {town} is so cold my fingers forgot how to type, sorry for the typos xD
Is it normal that the sky over {village} is that color or is it just me?? Asking for a friend who is also me :)
Someone told me the frost was a siege tactic and I believed them for three whole days. Please laugh with me, I am embarrassed :D
Lag is making my horse do a little dance every time I move, I think it is happy?? Hello everyone, I hope your day is warm!

player_joined_my_faction.text: Everyone please welcome {player} to {my_faction}!! They are way more experienced than me so please help them, and me too :) xD
Welcome to {my_faction} {player}. I am still learning where the good doors are, but I will show you what I know :)
{player} joined {my_faction}?? Okay, I was nervous about you before but now I think we can be friends, sorry for the silly face :P
{player}, I did not expect you to join us, honestly. I hope you do not mind if I still ask you lots of questions :(

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Yes yes yes, ser {player}, an alliance!! I have never had one before, so please be patient with my questions :D
Alright {player}, I accept. I am not sure what an alliance does exactly, but I think it means we wave at each other nicely :)
An alliance with you against {enemy_faction}, wonderful!! I will try not to get us both lost on the road, I promise :(
I accept, {player}. Just so you know, {rival} once pushed me into a ditch, so please keep them away from my wagon :(
Yes please ser {player}!! You hold my banner and I will hold yours, that is how alliances work right? I think I read it somewhere :)

captured_by_player.text: Oh no, you caught me ser {player}!! Please do not be too mean, I only have {gold} gold and most of it is for bread :(
Right, I am your prisoner now. Sorry, I did not see you coming through the frost. Is {gold} gold a fair price for me?? :)
Ser {player}, you caught me fair and square. I will not run, I promise, I am terrible at running anyway. Please talk to my {my_faction} friends about my ransom :D
This is very embarrassing ser {player}. All of {my_faction} will laugh at me for weeks, and it is all my fault for trusting that map. Please be quick??

ambient_trade.text: salt in {town} at {gold} gold a sack, fair weights, no tricks. anyone buying in bulk?
selling dyed wool out of {town}, {gold} gold the bolt. serious buyers only, i'm not chasing you.
looking to buy 40 sacks of grain near {town}, paying {gold} gold. the caravan is waiting.
wool in {town} has dropped to {gold} gold, which is a crime. holding my stock till it climbs back.
anyone need horses hauled to {town}? i'll take {gold} gold and deliver on time, every time.

encounter_trade_offer.text: {player}, i know you hate me, but a wagon of salt for {gold} gold beats a burned cart. think on it.
no hard feelings yet. {gold} gold for safe passage through {town}, and you keep your teeth. fair deal.
ser {player}, offer stands: {gold} gold for an escort into {town}. fair coin, no tolls on top.
could do {gold} gold for the road to {town}. not a bad rate for either of us, is it?
ah, {player}, for you it's {gold} gold and i'll throw in a bolt of wool. don't tell the others.

encounter_greeting.text: {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. your men are blocking my road and that's bad for both of us.
{player}, you're in my way and my wagons are heavy. move aside, or let's talk about what it costs.
ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. road's clear, my wagons are heavy, let's keep this friendly.
{player}! {persona} here, {my_faction} salt and wool. still got good wine for trade, or have you drunk it all?

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village}? that's a cart of wool gone and a season of trade lost. stop it, please.
{player}, you burned {village}. i can forgive a lot, but not a torched granary. talk to me.
burning {village} gets you nothing but a bad name on the roads, {player}. no one trades with arsonists.
{player}, {village} was a fair trade town. name your price for making it right and we'll see.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. every cart on those roads is now a target, great.
war with {enemy_faction} is official. my wool prices just went up, and not in my favor.
{my_faction} and {enemy_faction} at war again. the only winners here are the bandits.
sharpen your swords if you like, but my caravans will be taking the long road around {enemy_faction}.

peace_made.text: peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. the roads can breathe, and so can my ledger.
{my_faction} has made peace with {faction}. time to restock, the markets are finally sane again.
good news, the {my_faction} and {faction} treaty is signed. expect cheaper salt by the week's end.
with {faction} at peace, my wagons can finally use the old road. anyone want a ride to market?

released_by_player.text: {player} let me go without ransom? you've got my respect and a discount on wool for life.
thanks for letting me walk, {player}. a ransom is a fair number too, if you ever want one.
you released me, {player}, which is cheaper than my usual rate. i'll remember it.
{player} freed me for nothing. either you're soft or you're plotting something. either way, noted.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat my {troop_count} men at the ford. that battle cost me more than the road ever paid.
{player}, {troop_count} of my lads lost on the field. i'd rather we talk price than swords.
{player}, {troop_count} men gone and my wagons with them. well fought, but i still want my due.
a loss of {troop_count} troops, {player}. damn it. still, my coin is sound if you want a deal.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is at {fief}'s gates and my caravans are stuck. send help and i'll pay you well.
{player}, you're the only one i trust. {fief} is burning and {enemy_faction} won't stop. name your price.
ser {player}, {fief} won't hold against {enemy_faction} much longer. name a price and i'll meet it.
{player}, my friend, {fief} needs an escort or it's lost. the gold's in my strongbox, i swear on the wool.

ambient_complaint.text: {rival} is charging double for salt in {town}. that's not a market, that's robbery.
bandits on the {town} road again. my wagons are not free to replace, people.
{faction} tolls keep climbing and nobody's stopping it. my margins are bleeding out at the gates.
{rival} undercuts everyone and then cries when no one buys. no sympathy from this caravan.
every lord keeps starting wars over nothing. the {faction} lords especially. sort it out, please.

ambient_chatter.text: rain on the {town} road again. my wool's going soggy and my patience with it.
lag in {town} is wrecking my caravan timing. who's running the host, and can they fix it?
heard {village} has a new mill. might be worth a visit for the flour trade, if the prices hold.
the map says the {town} pass is clear. i'll believe it when my wagon gets through in one piece.
anyone else stuck at {village} for an hour? lost half a day and a wheel, fine way to start a week.

beat_player.text: Good field work, {player}. You kept your line when it mattered. Most would have broken at the ford.
You paid {troop_count} men for that hill, {player}. Come by after and I'll show you where you could have saved half.
{player}, you won this one. Enjoy it while the {gold} lasts. It does not buy a second chance at Castelnarc.
Charging downhill with {troop_count} men was never going to end well. I have the notebook to prove it.

beat_by_player.text: Well played, {player}. Hard to hold a line like that with only {troop_count} men. Good eye for the ground.
You had me on the flank, {player}. Come by after and I will walk you through where my {troop_count} went wrong.
Hm, {player}. You beat me today. In the first war I'd have lost the whole column that way. Still, the notebook keeps a count.
{player} won the day, and I lost {troop_count} men to a bad scout report. Note it, newcomers. Don't trust the scouts.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work with {player} today. {troop_count} men and not one reckless charge. That is how the fens were held, back in the first war.
That was clean, {player}. We broke {enemy_faction} because nobody ran ahead of the line. Buy the next round when we're back :)
{player}, you kept your place in the line. Good. Plenty of people forget that wars are won in the boring parts.
{enemy_faction} will remember that field for a while. Shared victories are the only kind I trust these days.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk instead of taking the ransom, {player}. I won't forget that. The next siege I run, you get the first seat.
{player} released me without ransom. Rare enough to mention. Ransom makes for tidier books, but mercy keeps the roads open.
Letting me go cost you a good ransom, {player}. Don't make a habit of it or the others will start expecting the same.
Gracious of {player} to let me walk. Most would have squeezed the purse. Remember that when your own turn comes.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome. Keep your head down for the first month and listen more than you talk.
So you've come to {my_faction}, {player}. Good. Read the old charters before you argue with anyone, they save a lot of grief.
{player}, {my_faction} is a long road for a man who has only just arrived. Prove the oath was not a convenience.
Be kind to the new ones, that's my rule. {player} will learn {my_faction} the slow way, like the rest of us.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} to {player}. Well earned, I think. The last holder lost it by being too eager. Learn from that.
You have {fief} now, {player}. I've held worse, and I've lost better. Keep the walls manned and the granary full.
{fief} went to {player}. I will not say the choice was wrong. I will say I kept my notes on the last three who held it.
Hm. {player} got {fief}. Let us see how long the walls stand before we start clapping.

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, at your service. Sit by the fire a moment, the road ahead is muddy and I have tea.
{player}. {persona}, {my_faction}. Your party is on the wrong side of the ridge, you know. Let me show you the way round.
{player}. We meet again on the map. Keep to your side of the river and we both get home for dinner.
Well met, {player}. {persona} here. Heard you were in the fens last season. Tell me it wasn't as bad as the rumors.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe road, {player}. Mind the bridge at the crossing, it has been sagging since the first war and nobody has fixed it.
That will do for now, {player}. We will meet again on the map. I'll be the one with a notebook.
Go on then, {player}. Keep your banners out of my fields and we shall have no trouble.
Until the next ridge, {player}. Eat something hot before you march, and keep your men dry.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road to {town} again. Anyone who says the fens have dried out has never walked them in autumn.
The granary in {village} is half empty this season. Bring grain before the price climbs and you'll thank yourself.
Notes for newcomers: a siege lasts longer than the first hour looks like it will. Plan supplies for three months.
Heard the bridge at {town} finally got repaired. Took a decade. We are a patient folk here.

player_big_defeat.text: Hard day, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men in one go happens to all of us. I lost a column at Castelnarc once.
I saw the field, {player}. A bad morning, not a finished campaign. Come by and I'll show you the notebook.
{player} lost most of the army near the ford. Scouts first, banners second, that's the old lesson. Write it down.
{troop_count} men gone, {player}. I told you the ridge was a trap. Rebuild and do not wave your banner so loudly next time.

war_declared.text: The council has voted for war with {enemy_faction}. I opposed it gently, which is why nobody heard me.
{my_faction} goes to war with {enemy_faction}. I did say the vote would be unanimous. I never said whose.
Banners are raised against {enemy_faction}. I have already drafted the letter explaining why it was all my idea.
Well. {enemy_faction} is now declared an enemy of {my_faction}. I shall write the wording myself, to be correct.

peace_made.text: Terms with {faction} are agreed. I brokered them over three dinners and will not be thanked for it.
{my_faction} and {faction} are at peace. Do ask me how, but only if you have an afternoon free.
The council accepted peace with {faction}. A fine result. Patience outlasted the swords, as it so often does.
Peace with {faction} is signed. Curious how some lords still call that a defeat.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. A wise choice, and a patient one. I am rather pleased.
Do come find me, {player}. There is much to discuss about {my_faction} before the next council.
{player} joins {my_faction}. I shall reserve judgement until I see how they vote.
{player}, you have joined {my_faction}. I wish you every success. I hope you read the charter first.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. I wish them joy of it. Loyalty is a luxury some can afford once.
You left us for {faction}, {player}. I shall not raise my voice. I never do, and you know why.
{player} has gone over to {faction}. Such moves are always discussed carefully, usually over wine.
I understand why you went to {faction}, {player}. Ambition is a poor master, yet an honest one.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} now holds {fief}. Well deserved, I think. I did argue for it, though I shall not say so loudly.
{fief} has gone to {player}. How generous the council feels this season. I wonder what was promised.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. I trust you will keep its ledgers in better order than the last steward.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. I would have liked a word first. Still, the council rarely asks me.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is no friend of ours, and I suspect {rival} has been counting on that.
Keep this between us, {player}. {enemy_faction} is a problem that patient people solve together.
{player}, {rival} has been undermining us both. Stand with me against {enemy_faction}. Let us see who is left.
I am offering this to you alone, {player}. A common stand against {enemy_faction} would be wise.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours again, taken from {enemy_faction} with hardly a death. Efficiency is a kind of mercy.
{my_faction} now holds {fief}. The council will be told it was a battle. I shall say it was a negotiation.
The banners of {my_faction} fly over {fief}. {enemy_faction} will mourn it and blame the weather.
{fief} has changed hands. Those who swore {enemy_faction} would never yield it were not paying attention.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. Bold. I do hope they enjoy the upkeep, which I shall mention at council.
{player}, you have {fief} now. I shall remember this, and so will the council, though only one of us says so.
{fief} changed hands under {player}. A clever move. I would call it sporting, if I were the sporting sort.
Well played, {player}, taking {fief}. I was fond of it, but I know a fair trade when I see one.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Yes, {player}, I accept. Against {enemy_faction} we shall do very well. Just keep {rival} from hearing of it first.
I accept your proposal, {player}. A useful arrangement. We shall see how it reads once the council has had its say.
Gladly, {player}. Let us make this formal before {enemy_faction} notices how well we get along.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I thank you for asking, but I have seen how you treat your allies. I would not wish that on mine.
I must decline, {player}. Not out of spite. My calendar is simply full of things {rival} has yet to explain.
I am sorry, {player}, but no. Our friendship is worth more than a hasty pact. Return when {rival} has left the room.
Refused, {player}. Pleasant as it is to be asked, I have not forgotten who sat silent during the last vote.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} has made the council benches damp again. Someone should complain, and I suppose it will be me.
Has anyone heard how {village} voted on the new road tolls? I have opinions, naturally, but I want theirs first.

Debts from the granary loans are never discussed in council. Some of us keep very good ledgers, all the same.

beat_player.text: A fine day of steel, {player}. I lost {troop_count} good men to that flank, but I would not have had it any other way :)
Those {troop_count} men were my own doing, not yours, {player}. Come find me on the road and I will show you where I went wrong :)
Well struck, {player}. Your flank came round faster than I expected, and I have not forgotten the last time a line held like that. Pull up a stool by my fire sometime, friend :)
{player} took {gold} from my purse today and I still call it a fair lesson :) Crap, I should have guarded the ford.

beat_by_player.text: Well done, {player}. I brought {troop_count} men and went home with a lesson in humility, the cheapest thing I buy :)

Hell of a fight, {player}. I will remember that charge longer than you will, and I say that with respect. Till the next field, then :)

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work at the crossing, {player}. {troop_count} of us held the line and not one broke. Lovely :)

Shields up on the ridge, everyone. {enemy_faction} will test us again soon, so keep your {troop_count} in line :)

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free, {player}, when a ransom would have filled your purse. That is the mark of a good soul, and I will not forget it :)
Three cheers for {player}, who let an old veteran go without a single coin asked. Mercy is rarer on this road than gold :)
Released without ransom, {player}. Noted. I owe you a meal by the fire, and I have a feeling you will not let me forget it :)
{player} released me rather than ransom me. A strange choice from a rival, but I will take the freedom and keep an eye on your roads :)

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}! Our banners are a little braver with you in the ranks. Ask me anything on the road :)
I am glad you swore to {my_faction}, {player}. Come find me when you have your bearings and I will show you the good campsites :)
{player} has joined {my_faction}. We will see what kind of soldier they make, though I suspect they will do well enough :)
So you have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Very well. Prove that oath on the field and I will have no complaint to make :)

player_granted_fief.text: Well earned, {player}! {fief} has been in worse hands, and I suspect it will be in better ones now. Hold it well :)
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. I cheered when the word came through, and I mean it. Come by when the walls need mending :)

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}! It warms my old bones to see you on the road. {persona} of {my_faction}, at your service :)
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here, riding a little slower than I used to. Mind the ruts on this stretch.
{player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, and I will be frank: our paths have crossed in ill temper before. Let us keep our swords sheathed today, shall we :)
Well met, {player}! I have ridden this road since the first war and still do not tire of the sight of a good party. {persona}, {my_faction}, pleased to see you.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. Keep your torches lit in the fens and your ranks tight on the moor. Until the next crossing :)
Fare well, {player}. The road is long and the weather is turning, so mind yourself out there.
Off you go then, {player}. I will not chase you today, but I will not forget that charge either :)
Go well, {player}. If you find yourself in trouble near the old bridge, send word and I will ride out myself :)

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. Mud in the boots, but the bread is still warm at the inn, so I call that a fair trade :)

war_declared.text: The council has been patient with {enemy_faction} for long enough. Now it has run out of patience, and so have I :)
{my_faction} has sent its regrets to {enemy_faction}. A pity they will only read them once the banners are up.
War with {enemy_faction}, then. I did say the council would come round eventually. Some of us always saw it coming.
Let it be recorded that {my_faction} tried diplomacy first. {enemy_faction} simply refused to listen, which is their own affair.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} is signed. Some of us arranged the terms while others were still shouting.
{faction} and {my_faction} have agreed to stop bleeding on each other. I suggested it weeks ago, in a corridor, quietly.
A treaty with {faction} is good for trade and better for my ledgers. Ask me about the clauses, if you can keep a secret.
Terms agreed with {faction}. The council will vote on them, of course, but the real vote was held in private :)

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome to the council's good graces, such as they are.
{player} now flies the colours of {my_faction}. I shall reserve judgement until the first vote, as is only proper.
{player}, I am glad you chose {my_faction}. Keep your ledgers tidy and your friends closer, as they say in Vignebel.
{player}, you took your time deciding. {my_faction} remembers who hesitated, and so do I, at length.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. How very brave of them to leave so loudly, and so early.
{player} has gone over to {faction}. Loyalty is a fine thing, provided it pays. I wish them every fortune.
{player}, you will find {faction} far less forgiving than I have been. Think on that before the next council.
{player}, I am sorry to see you go to {faction}. Should you tire of their company, my door is still open.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has been granted to {player}. Results are rewarded, it seems, and I did note that the council was listening.
So {player} holds {fief} now. A fine reward for a fine bit of lobbying, I am told. I was not asked, naturally.
{player}, {fief} is yours now. I hope its walls hold better than the promises that bought them.
{player}, congratulations on {fief}. Remember who spoke for you in the chamber. I certainly will.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {rival} has been promising {enemy_faction} our votes. I have a better offer, built on a shared grievance.
Between us, {player}, {enemy_faction} will not hold their ground past the spring council. Stand with me against {rival}.
{player}, you and I have always understood each other. {rival} does not, and that is their weakness. Shall we use it on {enemy_faction}?
{player}, a word in private. {rival} is telling everyone they are untouchable. Shall we find out how wrong they are?

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours again, taken from {enemy_faction} while they were busy with their feuds. {my_faction} rejoices, quietly.
The banners of {my_faction} now fly over {fief}. {enemy_faction} will be writing letters about this for months.
{fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. A fine day for the council, and an even finer day for my memory of who promised what.
Word is {fief} changed hands today, from {enemy_faction} to {my_faction}. I do enjoy it when plans come together.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief}. Clever, if you like your victories bought with other people's trust.
{fief} went to {player} this week. I shall be writing a strongly worded letter to the council, in my best hand.
{player}, you have {fief} now. Enjoy the walls. I shall enjoy watching how long you keep them.
{player}, {fief} was mine before it was yours. Do not worry, I keep track of such debts, and I always collect.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ah, {player}, I was hoping you would ask. Against {rival} and {enemy_faction} we shall make a fine pair. Shall we sign it now?
Very well, {player}. An alliance against {enemy_faction} suits me, and {rival} has been insufferable for some time.
{player}, you have always had a good eye for opportunity. I accept. Let the council hear of it only once it is done.
Agreed, {player}. We shall keep {rival} guessing, and {enemy_faction} will learn what patience costs them.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. You came to me with a proposal and no list of favours owed. I do not treat that as a serious offer.
I think not, {player}. {rival} would take it as a sign of weakness, and I cannot afford to look weak before the council.
Not today, {player}, I am sorry. Ask me again after the spring vote, and bring more than good intentions.
Your offer is noted, {player}, and so is the look on your face. I am not in the business of trusting loud bargainers.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, traveller, and hear the banner of Lauresse before you draw steel. I am {persona}, sworn to Corbanel, and I have not forgotten the fen raiders who burned my family's hall.
Good day, ser {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, riding the causeways as my grandsire swore I should. Let us see whether your road and mine run together.
Ser {player}, my heart lifts to see you upon this road. Tell me your business, for I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I would gladly share bread and tale with you.
You stand in the path of {my_faction}, ser {player}. Yield the road or prove your mettle, for {persona} will chronicle whichever you choose.

encounter_threatened.text: You would have {gold} from me? Then you must first pry it from my cold hands, ser {player}. Lauresse does not pay tribute to threats.
Ser {player}, a demand of {gold} is a bold word for a stranger on the causeway. Speak more plainly, and I shall answer as my oath requires.
Threaten me for {gold} and you shall have a tale worth telling, ser {player}. My grandsire fought worse men than you on the causeways of Corbanel.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for no friend of mine would name a price of {gold} with such a face. Let us speak of honour instead.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept, ser {player}, and gladly. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let the minstrels sing of this day.
Very well, ser {player}. An oath is sworn between us, and I shall keep mine to the last. Do not ask me to forgive {rival}, however.
By the honour of Lauresse, I take your hand, ser {player}. Together we shall break {enemy_faction}, and I will remember the service you do me.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. A banner of Lauresse does not march beside a stranger who has not earned its trust. Go and earn it, if you can.
I must decline, ser {player}. My oath is sworn to Corbanel alone, and I will not bind it to any road I have not walked.
I am grieved to refuse you, ser {player}, truly. Yet while {rival} still rides these causeways, I dare not promise what I cannot keep.
Propose an alliance to me? Ask {rival} to kneel first, ser {player}, and then we shall speak of oaths.

captured_by_player.text: Your blade has bested mine, ser {player}, and I stand as your captive. Name your ransom of {gold}, and know that {my_faction} will remember this humbling.
So the causeways have bound me. Very well, ser {player}, you have won this field, and I shall bear my captivity with what dignity remains to me.
A fair fight, ser {player}, and well fought. I am your prisoner now, and I would rather lose to you than to any fen raider. Name your terms.
Bind me, then, and be quick about it! The banner of Lauresse does not weep in chains, though {my_faction} shall surely pay {gold} to see me free.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me go without a ransom. I shall remember that mercy longer than any blade you ever raised.
Ser {player} has loosed me from chains without ransom. A rare grace on these causeways, and I will not forget it.
You spared me, ser {player}, but do not think this humbles me. Lauresse pays its debts, and this one I shall repay in steel.
Honour to ser {player}, who freed me without gold. The chronicle of Lauresse shall record it under mercy, not under ransom.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction} like a coward slinking off the field. Let the minstrels mock the deserter.
You turned your banner to {faction}, ser {player}, and {my_faction} is poorer for it. An oath broken is a stain no ballad will wash clean.
Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Such roads are open to all, yet honour does not travel as lightly as a rider does.
I bear you no grudge, ser {player}, though I grieve that your oath to {my_faction} is broken. May {faction} prove worthy of you.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has drawn sword against {enemy_faction}. The banner of Lauresse rides to war, and the fen raiders shall not sleep easy tonight.
Hear, all Ormerath: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war. Lauresse keeps its oath, and blood shall answer each lost hall.
Word has come that {enemy_faction} stands against {my_faction}. I ride to the causeways gladly, for my grandsire's oath demands it.
War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}! Let each honest blade sharpen its edge, for the chronicle of Lauresse is not yet finished.

fought_alongside_player.text: {troop_count} of the enemy fell today against {enemy_faction}, and ser {player} stood at my side like a true knight. Sing it!
Well struck, ser {player}. We bore {troop_count} men against {enemy_faction}, and the field is ours. I have no doubt the chroniclers will name this day rightly.
A hard-won field against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}, with {troop_count} of our number left standing. Honour enough for one day.

encounter_farewell.text: Fare you well, ser {player}. May your road be smooth and your oaths be kept, and should we meet again, I shall greet you with a full heart.
Until we cross paths again, ser {player}. Our roads part here, and I shall ride on with the banner held high.
Go, then, ser {player}, and count yourself lucky to leave with your purse. The next meeting shall be settled with steel, not courtesy.
Begone from my sight, ser {player}. I have marked your face and your name, and neither shall slip from my memory.

ambient_chatter.text: Mist lies thick over {village} this morning and the causeways run slick with dew. A poor day to ride, yet honour waits for no sunshine.
Ale at {town} tastes of home tonight, friends. I raise my cup to every rider who keeps faith on the long roads.
My grandsire crossed these marshes in a storm worse than this. Such weather tests a banner, and Lauresse has never lowered its own.
Pellegrane's towers were grey as slate when I rode past, and yet they stood. So too shall we, friends, if we hold firm.
Fen raiders have been seen near {village}. Keep your watch sharp and your blades ready, for I have seen what they leave behind.

Ser {player}, congratulations on {fief}. It is a considerable responsibility, and I am sure you will tell me all about it soon.

Ser {player}, {fief} is a fine prize. I hope its grain ledgers are in better order than the council's attendance records.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: Ser {player}, {rival} has been quietly working against us, and {enemy_faction} would welcome a friend in that quarter. Might we talk?
Ser {player}, consider an understanding against {rival} and their friends in {enemy_faction}. I would value your support in council.
Ser {player}, {rival} votes only for their own comfort. Let us arrange matters against {enemy_faction} between us, quietly.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {my_faction} has taken {fief} from {enemy_faction}. I trust the council will record the victory with proper ceremony.
The banners of {my_faction} now fly over {fief}, while {enemy_faction} sulks in its tents. A fine result for the council's strategy.
{fief} is in our hands after {enemy_faction}'s defeat there. I did recommend the campaign, though I shall not labour the point.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. Bold of them, though I shall recall every grain they owe before the next council sits.
Ser {player}, you have taken {fief} from our hold. I shall not forget it, and the council will hear every detail of it.
{fief} changed hands to {player} this week. Fortune favours the energetic, and I shall try to be energetic too.
Ser {player}, {fief} is yours now, I see. Do send word on how you intend to govern it, since the council will ask.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept. {rival} has been a thorn in the council for too long, and {enemy_faction} would be wise to take note of our arrangement.
Agreed, Ser {player}. We shall oppose {rival} together in council and let {enemy_faction} discover the consequences at its leisure.
Ser {player}, a gracious offer, and I accept it gladly. Between us we shall keep {rival} and {enemy_faction} thoroughly outvoted.

encounter_alliance_no.text: Ser {player}, I think not. I have seen how {rival} treats their friends, and I would rather not give them the chance.
Ser {player}, your offer is appreciated, but I must decline. The council has not yet decided where {rival} stands, and I will not commit before then.
Ser {player}, I am flattered, truly. Yet I cannot tie myself to anything while {rival} still sits on the regency bench, so forgive me.

ambient_chatter.text: The roads out of {town} are muddy again, and the council has still not approved the repairs. Shall the carts simply sink, then?
Has anyone heard from {village} about the harvest? I would like a clear account before the next vote, if anyone can spare the time.
The weather over {town} is dreadful, yet the minutes still arrive on time. Some small mercies are worth recording, I think.
I am told {village} has a new reeve, and I intend to write to him at once. Proper introductions matter far more than people admit.

ambient_trade.text: Wool bales going for 40 gold in {town} this week. Fair weight, no clipping :)
Salt is selling at {gold} a sack in {town}. Anyone bound for the Pellegrane road, now is the time to buy.
Buying good hides in {town}, paying {gold} on the spot. Fair dealing, as always.
Caravan leaving {town} at dawn with spare room for two carts. Share the road fee and we both save.
Quick sales on dyed cloth in {town}. Name a price within reason and I will meet you halfway.

encounter_trade_offer.text: Ser {player}, I do not trade with raiders, but {gold} for the salt at {town} is a fair number. Speak plainly if you want it.
Ser {player}, {gold} for the wool delivered to {town}? That is a fair offer and I will take it if the weight holds.
Ah, {player}, you have a nose for profit! {gold} for the whole lot in {town} and we both walk away richer. Shake on it?

encounter_greeting.text: Stay back, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}, and my wagons are not for raiders.
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, traveling the Pellegrane road. Nothing to fear here unless you carry a toll receipt I am missing.
{player}! {persona} of {my_faction} here. Fancy meeting you on the road. Any salt to spare, or are you only passing through with empty carts?

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village} and I lost three carts of wool to the smoke. Every fire you light costs the whole road money.
Ser {player}, {village} is ash now. Name your price for the damages and we can talk business instead of blades.
Raids on {village} cost us all a fortune in lost wool, {player}. Ledger is open and I am keeping score.
{player}, the burning of {village} was bad for trade on everyone's road. Let us settle it with coin before the bandits notice.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} is at war with {enemy_faction}. Good for the swordsmiths, terrible for the rest of us with carts on the road.
War with {enemy_faction} means tolls on every bridge will climb by midsummer. Someone explain the logic to me, please.
Fine, {my_faction} has declared on {enemy_faction}. My wool prices are already rising and my patience is shorter than my margins.
Caravans bound for {enemy_faction} lands are suspended until further notice. Buy your salt early, the road will be dear.
{enemy_faction} and {my_faction} at each other's throats again. Stock up now, because in a war prices only climb.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. Roads reopen and my drivers can sleep again. Very good news.
Finally, {my_faction} has made peace with {faction}. Expect cheaper salt on the Pellegrane road by the next market day.
Terms agreed between {my_faction} and {faction}. I have already booked three caravans for the reopened routes.
Ink is dry on the treaty with {faction}. Wool, bread and salt move freely again, and I can finally stop counting tolls in my sleep.

released_by_player.text: Thank you, {player}, for letting me go without a ransom. I will remember the courtesy, and maybe the next wool shipment too.
{player}, you let me walk free instead of asking for gold. That is a rare kind of deal and I will return the favor on the road.
{player} released me without ransom. A strange choice, but I will not complain. A free cart is a good cart.
{player}, you spared me the ransom. Do not think this makes us friends, but I owe you one and I always pay my debts.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat us in the field with {troop_count} troops. Forty good men lost on bad ground. Expensive lesson, that.

You won this one, {player}, with {troop_count} men against my lot. Do not expect me to thank you for it, but I will count the cost.
{player} took the field with {troop_count} troops and beat us fair. I still want my wagons back, but I respect the win.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing on {fief} and my caravans are stuck behind it. Can you spare a few men? I will pay well.
My friend {player}, {fief} is under threat from {enemy_faction}. Help me hold it and the next salt shipment is yours at cost.
{player}, I need your swords at {fief} before {enemy_faction} takes the bridge. Name a fair price and I will meet it.
{player}, {enemy_faction} will strangle the road to {fief} if we do nothing. Would you ride with me? Bread and wool are at stake.

ambient_complaint.text: Tolls at {town} jumped overnight. Bandits eat my profits, then the toll keeper eats what is left.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, ser {player}! I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I bid you stand aside before the road is closed to you.
Good morrow, ser {player}. {persona} rides for {my_faction} this dawn, as my house has ridden these roads for three generations.
Ser {player}, what a joy to meet a traveller of honour upon these roads. Walk with me a while and let us speak of old oaths.
The ancestors of my house look down upon this meeting, ser {player}. Choose your next words with care, for they will be remembered.

encounter_threatened.text: You name a price of {gold} gold for my passage, ser {player}? My house does not pay tribute on its own road. Come and take it if you dare.
Threats ring hollow in my ears, ser {player}. I will not surrender a single coin of the {gold} you demand, though I would hear your reasons.
By the blood of my ancestors, ser {player}, you demand {gold} as though honour were a thing for sale. I shall not sell it.
I hold you in regard, ser {player}, so I will speak plainly. Demanding {gold} gold of me is a poor opening to any friendship.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept, ser {player}. Let our standards stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let the saga record that we did so willingly.
Very well, ser {player}. An alliance sworn before witnesses binds me, and I shall hold to it for as long as your word holds true.
Gladly I take your hand, ser {player}. Against {enemy_faction} we ride as one, and {rival} shall learn what honour looks like.
Accepted. Know that I trust you only as far as your word carries, ser {player}, and I shall watch every step you take beside me.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. I will not bind my name to yours. The house of Garrouse does not ally with those who sell their word to the highest bidder.
I must decline, ser {player}. My oath does not permit me to ride beside one who has not yet earned my trust.
My heart is warm toward you, ser {player}, but I cannot pledge to you yet. Prove your word upon the road and ask me again.
Seek such company from {rival}, ser {player}. My banner will not stand beside a flag that changes with every wind.

captured_by_player.text: You have taken me, ser {player}, and I will not kneel to you. Name your ransom of {gold} gold, and {my_faction} will pay it when next our roads cross.
So fortune has turned against me at the ford, ser {player}. Speak your terms plainly, and I shall hear them with a steady face.
A fair blow was struck, ser {player}, and I bear no shame for it. Keep me in honour, and I shall not forget your courtesy.
Chains do not break a Garrouse oath, ser {player}. Hold me as long as you wish; my tongue remains my own and my ancestors remain my witnesses.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you could have ransomed me and chose mercy instead. My house will remember that gift for generations to come.
Ser {player} has loosed a captive without ransom. Let all who ride these roads know that honour still walks among us.
You released me, ser {player}. I do not yet know whether to call it mercy or folly, but I thank you for it all the same.
Ser {player} let me go without ransom. Mercy is a debt I will repay, though I have not yet decided on the coin.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has abandoned {my_faction} for {faction}. A banner unfurled in haste is a banner soon torn, mark my words.
You turned your back on {my_faction}, ser {player}, and rode to {faction}. Such a choice will be sung of in the hall for a long time.
Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Each man must answer to his own conscience, though I shall weigh this one carefully.
I grieve to see you leave {my_faction}, ser {player}. Whatever oath you swore to {faction}, I pray you keep it better than this.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war upon {enemy_faction}. Let the roads run red and the saga be written in iron, for our ancestors demand it.
Hear this, all of Ormerath: {my_faction} takes up arms against {enemy_faction}. Our standards shall answer for every insult borne.
The horn has sounded, and {my_faction} stands against {enemy_faction}. I ride at dawn with my oath upon my shoulder.
War with {enemy_faction} is declared, and {my_faction} shall not flinch. Let no bard say our house hid behind its walls.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, we stood together and {troop_count} of {enemy_faction}'s finest fell before us. Such a field deserves a song, and I shall sing it.
{troop_count} of {enemy_faction} lie broken on the field, and ser {player} fought at my side. Honour was served this day.
Ser {player}, your sword arm was a true blessing today. Those {troop_count} soldiers of {enemy_faction} will not forget it either.
You fought well at my flank, ser {player}. We broke {troop_count} of {enemy_faction}, and I grant you a measure of respect for it.

encounter_farewell.text: Fare you well, ser {player}. May the road keep your horse sure and your word sound until we meet again upon these hills.
Go in peace, ser {player}. I shall ride my dawn chapter onward, and you shall have a place in its telling.
Begone for now, ser {player}. Our reckoning is not finished, and the ancestors have not yet tired of watching us both.
We part, ser {player}, but not as friends. I shall remember this meeting every time I cross the ford.

ambient_chatter.text: The mist lies heavy over {village} this dawn. I ride its roads still, and every ride is a chapter in my house's long saga.
Good folk of {town}, keep your banners dry and your oaths dry too. Rain washes away lesser promises, or so my grandmother said.
A fine morning for the old roads. I have ridden from {village} to {town} with my ancestors at my back, and I feel them smiling.
Do the wagons still run from {town} to {village} this week? I would have fresh bread before the next chapter of my ride.
