{gold} banked and not one coin spent without a return calculation. the rest of you are guessing

my_faction_took_fief.text: {my_faction} took {fief} from {enemy_faction}. garrison math was right and the siege was clean. next target already counted
{fief} is ours now. {enemy_faction} fought it at the wrong ratio and lost the gate first. predictable
{my_faction} holds {fief}. the siege took eleven minutes by my clock. {enemy_faction} should check its numbers

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} is sieging {fief}. good. the garrison is sized to outlast them and their ram count is wrong for that wall
{player}, you are sieging {fief} with that formation. i have counted your rams. you will lose the gate by the third hour
{player} started a siege on {fief}. standard approach, slow and the wrong ratio for the wall. watch the timing
{player}, {fief} is held by a garrison i sized myself. go ahead and test it. i will have the breakdown posted after

ambient_chatter.text: the rain on the road to {town} is costing everyone speed. move the supply wagons earlier and stop complaining
{village} has the best grain yield on the map and nobody is using it. the price difference is obvious if you check
server lag again. the timing windows are unreliable this week and i am not blaming the players for that
anyone tracking the cavalry ratio on the {town} route. the numbers shifted after last patch and i want a second opinion

beat_player.text: {troop_count} troops and no flank. Your line folded on the second charge, {player}. Fix the spacing.
Wrong, {player}. Your reserve sat idle for six minutes. Idle troops are the cheapest loss there is. gg.
Good fight, {player}. Your flank timing slipped at the ford and cost you {troop_count} men. My push landed on schedule. Sort the spacing next time and you will be dangerous.

beat_by_player.text: My archers were out of position on that flank, {player}. Lost {troop_count} to a timing error. That is not the same as losing the fight.
Your push came in 40 seconds early by my count, {player}. I had the timing right and the positioning wrong. Rematch when I fix it.
Clean fight, {player}. I lost {troop_count} to a flank I should have covered. My spreadsheet says the gap was three ranks wide. I will close it before the next siege.

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} again. {troop_count} troops and a spreadsheet full of gaps. Counting this as a grudge now.
That is the third time, {player}. I have the logs. The timing is sound, so the flank is where I will find the gap.
Third loss to you, {player}. Honest read: you read my line better than I read yours. I am still correcting the ratios.

player_win_streak.text: {player} is on a streak and everyone keeps saying luck. It is not luck. Look at the flank timing and stop calling it chance.
Your streak is real, {player}. Most of it is ratio discipline, the rest is you not overextending. I respect the discipline.
Keep it up, {player}. Streaks break on the flank, and I have a fix for you if you want it.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of the army and is calling it bad luck. The flank was empty and the reserve came too late. Fix it.
Rough day, {player}. {troop_count} troops gone to a unit sent into a corner. Send your archers wider next time.
Bad field, {player}. The math still says your army was sound. Tell me what went wrong and I will tell you what I would have done.

whisper_challenge.text: {player}, meet me at {village} at dawn with equal numbers. I have the timing worked out. Clean terms, no excuses.
{player}, you owe me a clean field. Meet at {town} before noon. I bring the spreadsheet, you bring the archers.
{player}, {town} is open ground with a clean approach. Meet me there. I want to test the gap I found in your last formation.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} held the ridge while my second line closed on {enemy_faction}. Good ratio, {troop_count} men, clean finish.
Nice work on the flank, {player}. The timing held and your line did not break. Good to have you on my side for once.
We split {enemy_faction} clean, {player}. {troop_count} men on the line and not one caught out of position. Do the same at the next siege and we keep this ratio.

ambient_brag.text: {fief} garrison is at {troop_count} men and {gold} gold in the coffers. Efficient, as always. Not bragging, just reporting.
Ran the numbers on the last siege. {troop_count} men, {fief} taken before dawn, costs under budget. The spreadsheet is never wrong.
{gold} gold and {troop_count} troops, with no wasted ranks. Anyone still fielding a loose line is paying for it.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours. {my_faction} took it from {enemy_faction} before dawn with the flank timed to the second. Clean capture.
Captured {fief} for {my_faction}. Their reserve was three ranks late. Nothing to talk about, the numbers did the work.
{fief} changed hands. {my_faction} push came in on schedule, {enemy_faction} did not expect it. Ratios favored us from the start.

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} is sieging {fief}. Check the walls, the approach has a gap on the east side. Try not to waste it, {player}.
{player}, you started a siege on {fief} with the wrong ratio. I have the numbers. Lift it before you lose the men.
Siege on {fief}, {player}. I will hold it. Come back when your ratios are better and I will show you where the wall fails.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. Bad for archers, good for the slow ones. Nothing to fix about that.
Lag at {village} is killing the flank timing. Someone should look at the server before the next siege.
Anyone else notice the map pins near {village} are off by a tile? Spreadsheet says the road is shorter than we think.

encounter_greeting.text: oh no oh no, are you the ser that {my_faction} keeps warning me about?? sorry :( im only a newbie, pls dont hit me
hello {player}! im {persona} of {my_faction} and this is my first time on the road so pls be gentle xD
{player}!!! you are the nicest looking ser i have seen all day :D can we walk the same way for a bit? i wont slow you down :)

beat_by_player.text: oh no... {player} you have {troop_count} men?? i counted badly again :( i guess that was a loss lol
{player} beat us with {troop_count} troops!! i think i am bad at this game lol :D
hi {player}, sorry about the fight :( {troop_count} troops is a lot for a newbie. could you teach me the basics some time?

released_by_player.text: thank you thank you {player}!! you let me go?? i owe you one, i really mean it :D
{player} let me go instead of asking for a ransom!! i am still shocked lol. nice ser :)
{player} why did you let me go?? i thought captives had to pay. sorry if i did something wrong :(

fought_alongside_player.text: we did it with {player} and {troop_count} troops!!! i am still shaking :D so cool
{player} you were amazing out there!! i think i just ran where you ran :D thank you so much
good fight {player}!! against {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} men? i honestly thought we would lose :)

whisper_beg_help.text: {player} pls, {fief} is getting attacked by {enemy_faction} and i dont know what to do :( could you come help? i can carry a spear i think
hi {player}, sorry to ask, {enemy_faction} is at {fief} and we are losing. would you be able to lend a hand? no pressure :)
{player}!! sorry sorry, i think {fief} is about to fall to {enemy_faction}. you are the only ser i know who can help :(

ambient_lfg.text: looking for a few ser to hit {enemy_faction} at {fief}, newbies welcome :D i will bring the spears!!
{my_faction} needs people for a siege at {fief}!! i dont know how sieges work but i can carry things :)
lfg for {fief} vs {enemy_faction}, all skill levels welcome (i am very low skill lol) :D

ambient_chatter.text: is it just me or does the road to {town} go in circles?? i have walked it 3 times xD
why are my men so hungry?? is that normal?? sorry i am asking everything today :D
the weather near {village} is so pretty today!! i got rained on and still got lost lol

player_joined_my_faction.text: I JOINED {my_faction}!! thank you for having me, i will try not to get lost :D
hi {player}!! i just swore to {my_faction}, is it ok if i stay near you? i am so nervous :)
{player} just joined {my_faction}!! welcome me please if you see me wandering around lost :D

encounter_alliance_yes.text: yes yes yes {player}!! an alliance?? i dont know exactly what that means but i say yes :D
oh okay, an alliance with you {player}? sure! i will tell my people. sorry if i say the wrong thing :)
{player} thank you for asking me!! i was scared to talk to anyone. {rival} looks a bit scary though xD

captured_by_player.text: oh no, you caught me?? please dont hit me {player} :( i only have {gold} gold, you can take it all
ok ok, you win {player}. so i am a prisoner now?? how long do i have to stay? sorry for the trouble :)
{player} you got me!! that was the best fight of my life :D {my_faction} will be so jealous. {gold} gold is in my pouch

beat_player.text: {player} won the field with {troop_count} men. I lost ground today and I will learn from it, as I did in the first war.
Well fought, {player}. You took {gold} in spoils, and my men will remember the lesson. Come find me at the Imzaz ford.
You have the better of me this day, {player}. Do not mistake one field for the whole war. Spring water is patient and so am I.
Do not look so pleased, {player}. You earned those {gold} coins fairly, and I would rather lose to you than to a cheat.

beat_by_player.text: I lost {troop_count} men to {player} at the salt pans today. Good ground was taken by a good hand, and I bear no grudge.
A fair field, {player}. I have given up {troop_count} men and some pride, but the pride will mend faster than the men.
Well struck, {player}. I did not expect you to press so hard from the eastern dunes. Shake my hand before you ride off, and the water is on me.
{player} has beaten me again. Mark my words, I will be back on that ground with more patience and sharper spears.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and I held the line against {enemy_faction} today with {troop_count} men between us. That is how the old wars were won.
You fought like a veteran out there, {player}. The ground we took together is ground we both keep now.
We hold the same side for once, {player}. Keep your shield up and your eyes on {enemy_faction}, and we will talk of this at the ford.
Good work with {troop_count} men at the ridge. {enemy_faction} will remember that they met two stubborn banners today.

released_by_player.text: You could have named a ransom, {player}, yet you opened the gate instead. I will not forget that mercy.
{player} let me walk free from the cells today. Few would have done so, and fewer still without asking for a price.
Do not think this buys you my friendship, {player}. A released captive remembers the one who freed him, and I remember you.
Mercy in the field is rarer than good salt, {player}. I owe you a cup of mead at the ford when you next pass through.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Our banners have room for those who learn to stand their ground, and you look like you will.
I am glad you swore to {my_faction}, {player}. Come find me at the Imzaz ford in the evening and I will show you the old paths.
You have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Judge the oath by what you do in the coming seasons, not by what you say today.
{player} now bears the colors of {my_faction}. I will watch how you carry them, and I expect nothing less than honest work.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} is in good hands, {player}. I have seen many lords fall from too much land, so guard it well and the people will guard you.
The lord granted you {fief}, {player}. I am not one to grumble over the ledger, but I held that ground longer than you did.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. I will hold my tongue for now, but I will watch the walls you build and the men you keep.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. The first winter in a new keep teaches more than any tutor, so start early and listen.

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}, good to see a friendly banner on this road. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Water is short out here, so share it freely.
{player}, we meet on the open road. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. Keep your distance and we will have no quarrel today.
{player}. I know your banner, and I know your name. {persona} of {my_faction} does not forget a field where my men bled. Ride carefully.
Steady, {player}, I see your party on the road. It is {persona} here, of {my_faction}. Let us trade news before the sun dips.

encounter_farewell.text: Go safely, {player}. May your water hold and your horses stay sound until we meet at the ford again.
We have talked enough for one day, {player}. Ride on, and mind the dunes where the sand swallows careless riders.
Our road parts here, {player}. Do not let it cross mine again without a good reason, for I have not forgotten you.
Farewell, {player}. Take a cup of water with you from the ford, and remember that the long road is kinder to patient men.

ambient_chatter.text: The heat over {town} is thick today. I have crossed the salt pans in worse, but my lips still crack by midday.
Word from {village} says the wells are running low again. Desert folk know this country well, so bring spare skins.
The fog came down over the marsh near {village} this morning, and I trusted my boots over my eyes.
Those who ride to {town} should take the eastern road, where the dunes hide less thirst. I have walked it many times.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost nearly all of {troop_count} men in that valley. Such a day breaks some captains, so rest and regroup before you march again.
Do not let today's loss weigh on you, {player}. I lost a full company once in the first war and still I went back to the field.
A hard blow for {player} today, with {troop_count} men gone from the rolls. Count what remains, take the lessons, and carry on.

war_declared.text: The council has voted, and {my_faction} now stands against {enemy_faction}. I did say it would come to this, did I not?
Such a shame that {enemy_faction} chose the sword over the ballot. I shall be sure the minutes reflect who insisted on it.
War with {enemy_faction} is declared. Every fief they hold is now a question for the council, and I have drafted the motion.
Let no one say {my_faction} rushed into this. We waited, we counted our friends, and only then did we count their soldiers.
{enemy_faction} will learn what a council can do when its patience runs out. Ser, I do hope they enjoy the rain.

peace_made.text: Peace with {faction} is signed, and I confess I drafted the terms before the ink was dry. Do try to look surprised.
{my_faction} and {faction} are at peace. Nothing reconciles a realm like a shared debt, and I hold most of theirs.
A truce with {faction} is in place. Let the lords who called me reckless now explain why the roads are open again.
So {my_faction} sheathes its blades for {faction}. How considerate of them to wait until my treaty was ready.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome, Ser, I always knew a good mind would find its way to the council.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. You will find the council warm, and I expect you will remember who opened the door for you.
You have joined {my_faction}, {player}. I trust you will weigh our offer as carefully as I weigh the favours you now owe.
{player} now wears the colours of {my_faction}. I shall not pretend I am pleased, though I am certainly not surprised.
So you have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Do keep your dagger sheathed in council, I would hate to see the minutes stained.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has abandoned {my_faction} for {faction}. A pity. Loyalty is such a fragile thing when the purse is heavier elsewhere.
You left {my_faction} for {faction}, {player}. I shall not forget, and neither will the council come the next tally.
{player} has taken their banners to {faction}. Ser, I wish them well, and I have already noted which of their friends stayed behind.
Ser {player}, you may leave {my_faction} for {faction} if you must, but do tell me first. I would rather lose you with dignity.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been given {fief}. Marvellous. I do wonder what they promised the steward, for I certainly did not offer him enough.
{fief} now answers to {player}. A fine choice by the council, though I shall be watching which votes come with it.
Congratulations to {player} on {fief}. Every good lord needs a seat to sit in, and I am glad the council found one for them.
{fief} is yours, {player}, and I was delighted to back you. Remember that such gifts are always noted in my ledger.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. Do enjoy the walls, Ser. I shall be counting on you to remember who spoke for you.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {rival} has been speaking ill of you in council, {player}, and I thought you deserved to know. Ally with me against {enemy_faction}?
Between us, {player}, {enemy_faction} will fall whether we hurry or not. Standing with me now means a seat at the table when they do.
{rival} and I have never quite agreed on anything, {player}. Against {enemy_faction}, however, I suspect we could.
Say the word, {player}, and I will bring {enemy_faction}'s grievances to the council under your name. Shall we?

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours at last. {enemy_faction} held it with a sword and a sulk, {my_faction} took it with a patient vote.
The banners of {my_faction} now fly over {fief}. I do hope {enemy_faction} enjoyed the siege, it cost them the town.
{fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. A small victory, Ser, but the council likes small victories it can count.
Sound the horns, {fief} belongs to {my_faction} now. I shall draft the thanks to the captain and the bill to {enemy_faction}.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. Very bold. I shall remember who bled for it, and who only rode in afterwards.
You have taken {fief}, {player}. Enjoy it while the council still lets you. These walls were never truly yours.
{fief} has changed hands to {player}. Shall we call it a clean campaign, or shall the council have a word about it?
{player}, {fief} was ours until this morning. I bear no grudge, Ser, only a quiet note in the ledger.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, you have a fine instinct for timing. Yes, let us stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let {rival} find out from the minutes.
I accept, {player}. Our banners will look well together over the field, and {rival} will have a long while to wonder how we agreed so quickly.
Very well, {player}, you have my hand. {enemy_faction} will regret the day it ignored our small league, and {rival} will regret ignoring us more.
Agreed, Ser {player}. We shall sign the pact before the council sits, and when {rival} asks why, I shall tell them the truth: we are simply more useful together.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I think not, {player}. Your offer is generous, but I have seen how your last alliance ended, and {rival} would not thank me for the company.
Not today, Ser {player}. Come back when I have counted the votes and know who is worth the trouble. {rival} is busy enough without us.
I must decline, {player}, though it pains me. The council has already promised {rival} a seat, and I would rather keep you as a friend than a rival.
Tempting, {player}, but I have an arrangement with {rival} that I cannot break in the open. Ask me again after the next vote.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. I swear the clouds keep better hours than the council does.
Has anyone seen the road to {village} this week? Half the carts are stuck, and the other half are carrying gossip.
The harvest in {village} is poor, which means the tithe will be late, which means someone will need a quiet word with the reeve.
Lag again on the eastern road. Ser, I cannot tell whether the server is slow or the rival lords are simply too busy lying.
If anyone needs me, I shall be in the hall counting favours. Do not tell the bards, they will only ask for a fee.

beat_player.text: We took {troop_count} men off that road today. Nobody here needs to make more of it than it was. Mind your wells, friend.
You came at my flank like a captain who never learned to guard his wells, {player}. I took {troop_count} of yours. Think on that before the next march.
Ser {player}, you pushed me hard and I will say so at every fire on the road. The first war taught me to respect a line that does not break easily.

beat_by_player.text: Your timing was sharp, {player}. I lost {troop_count} men to a flank I should have seen coming. Well played.
You beat me fair, {player}. Mind your own wells now, and I will be watching your next march with respect.
I forgive slowly, {player}, but I will remember that ambush. Losing {troop_count} men hurts, and you knew exactly where it would hurt most.
Ser {player}, I have walked these roads since the first war and I still learn something from every loss. You taught me a new trick today, and I thank you for it.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and I broke {enemy_faction} at the ford with {troop_count} men. Good work, and good ground choice. I say it plainly.
We held together well, {player}. I have not fought beside a captain that calm since the old wars. Let us do it again soon.
Ser {player}, we held the line against {enemy_faction} and you never needed me to tell you where to stand. That is rare. Guard your wells and we will get along fine.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free, {player}, when a ransom would have been the easy choice. I will not forget that mercy at the next council.
{player} released me from captivity without asking for ransom. A rare kindness on the salt roads, and old hands will speak of it.
I thank you for the release, {player}. Mercy is worth more to me than any coin, and I will remember it.
{player} let me go without ransom. I accept the kindness, grudgingly, and I still count you among those who owe this realm a lesson.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The road is long but the company is worth it. Ask me anything and I will answer honestly.
You swore to {my_faction} and I believe you mean it, {player}. I will show you where the wells are kept, and where the traps are.
{player} has joined {my_faction}. We will see how you hold up in the next siege, though I am not one to judge a captain by his first week.
Joining {my_faction} does not buy you my trust, {player}. Prove yourself on the road and I may forgive you in time.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} is a fine holding, {player}. Our lord chose well, and I expect you to keep its wells full through the dry months.
So you have {fief}, {player}. I hope you remember that a town is only as strong as the wells beneath its walls.
{fief} goes to {player}. I have held better ground for less honor in the old wars, and I say that without rancor, mostly.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Come find me when the first harvest is in and we will talk over what it needs.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Your party looks well fed, and that is the first sign of a good captain on the salt road.
Good day, Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}. Keep your distance and we shall get on well enough on this road.
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I remember your banners from Iggoudar, and I have not forgotten the truce. Keep your men back.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe roads, Ser {player}. Next time we meet, I will bring the good salt and you bring the stories.
Fare well, Ser {player}. The road is long, and so are the memories of this realm.
Off you go, Ser {player}. Mind the ford on your way, and do not test my patience on it again.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has come early to {town} this year. Old hands say that means a hard winter on the salt roads, so stock your wells now.
Heard that {village} has finally repaired its granary bridge. Good news for the road traders, and a relief to my old carts.
The north road out of {town} is quieter than it has been in years. Bring a spare horse anyway, because quiet roads have a way of changing.
I walked the first war roads near {village} as a young captain. The old stones still hold, if you know where to put your feet.

player_big_defeat.text: Hard luck, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men in one afternoon is a bitter thing, but many captains have rebuilt from less. Take heart.
I heard of the rout, {player}. Come sit at my fire when you are ready. I lost whole companies once and still walked home.
{player} lost most of their army and I will not pretend it is unfamiliar. Rebuild quietly, and the roads will forget.
I am sorry to hear of the rout, {player}. I will not gloat, though some on the road will. Learn from it and you may yet earn respect.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has put its name to this war, and I trust the council will remember who argued for patience first.
So {enemy_faction} wants a war. The council sits tonight, and I will be the one holding the minutes.
Swords are drawn against {enemy_faction}. Funny how the loudest voices in the hall always find battle easiest to fund.
We are at war with {enemy_faction}. I hope the lords who voted for this have also budgeted for the grain.

peace_made.text: Terms agreed with {faction}. Some of our hot-headed barons will sulk for a season, but they will come round.
{my_faction} and {faction} have signed. Peace suits the merchants and the people, and happens to suit my ledgers too.
A truce with {faction} at last. The council will call it wisdom. I would call it a sensible delay.
The peace with {faction} is sealed. Credit to the few who kept talking when the rest of the hall wanted blood.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The hall is richer for your sword, and I have already drafted your seat.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. I am sure they will find the council's rules are not so dull once learned.
{player}, you have chosen well. Come find me after the next session and we shall discuss what you are owed.
{player}, the oath is taken. I shall be watching how you keep it, as the council will.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has gone over to {faction}. A pity. Some of us will remember the ones who run at the first better offer.
{player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Ambition is a fine thing, though it makes people forgetful of old friends.
{player}, I shall not pretend I am surprised. I simply wish you had told me before the rest of the hall heard it.
I bear you no grudge, {player}. Whatever {faction} promised, I hope it was written down.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has gone to {player}. Congratulations are in order, though I did wonder whether the council was asked.
{player} now holds {fief}. Generous of our ruler. I shall be curious how long the gift lasts.
{player}, {fief} is yours now. Enjoy it while the council is still polite about it.
{player}, {fief} suits you. A fine seat, and the lords will need someone to answer to. Let us talk about that.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {rival} takes every lord's silence for consent. Care to join me against {enemy_faction} before they move?
{player}, I have a proposal for the two of us. {enemy_faction} is weaker than their speeches. Shall we speak tonight?
{player}, you and I would do well together against {enemy_faction}. Say the word and I will bring the papers.
{player}, I hear {rival} has been whispering about you in the hall. A quiet pact against {enemy_faction} might change that.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours. {enemy_faction} will mourn it in their own fashion, but the gates belong to {my_faction} now.
The banners of {my_faction} fly over {fief} at last. I am told {enemy_faction} took it rather badly.
{fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. A fine result for the council, and a small reminder to {enemy_faction} of what patience costs.
Good news from {fief}. {enemy_faction} lost it, {my_faction} gained it, and I shall expect proper thanks in the minutes.

player_took_my_fief.text: {fief} has been taken by {player}. Well done, I suppose. I shall be sure to remember whose sword did the work.
{player} has taken {fief}. I had my reasons for not defending it, but I expect the council will want an explanation.
{player}, {fief} was mine, and you have taken it. Do not imagine I have forgotten.
{player}, a fine campaign for {fief}. I only wonder whether you intend to keep it, or merely hold it until the next vote.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Agreed, {player}. We shall stand together against {enemy_faction}, and {rival} can find someone else to flatter.

{gold} spent on that army and {player} still folded to a flank. not a budget problem, a comp problem

beat_by_player.text: lost {troop_count} to {player}. my archers were out of position when the flank went. that's on me and it's getting fixed
{player} that cav mix was a counter i should have seen. i'm rerunning the fight tonight. don't get comfortable
{player} your ratio beat mine. my archers were out of position when the line bent. i'll recount and come back with numbers
{player} gg. {troop_count} men and you still read the flank. my reserve timing was off by a full charge

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} again. third time, {troop_count} men and the same flank gap. i'm not calling it luck anymore
{player} i have your last three fights in a sheet. the numbers are not in your favor forever
another loss to {player} with {troop_count} on the field. the rerun shows the same gap every time. i'll find it
{player} third loss to your comp. i hate the result. the reruns say your spacing is correct and mine isn't

player_win_streak.text: {player} is on a long run. either the meta is broken or they count better than everyone here. i think it's the second
{player} your streak is getting attention on the server. keep the mix tight and it won't end soon
{player} streak is not luck. every fight has the same cav-to-pike spacing. copy it or keep losing to it
{player} the streak ends when i say it does. i've got a rerun queued on your last three fights
{player} on a run and the comps are clean. not going to pretend that doesn't impress me

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of {troop_count} to someone else. the numbers were never going to hold with that flank open
{player} that loss was a bad mix, not bad luck. i've seen the replay. i can help fix the ratio if you want
{player} got rolled. {troop_count} men gone and the comp was the reason. recheck before you queue again
{player} you were outnumbered in the right places and under-stacked in the wrong ones. saw the whole field

whisper_challenge.text: {player} meet me at {town} with your full mix. no retreat and no reserve tricks. the numbers decide it
{player} {village} at dawn. i want a clean rematch with equal troop counts and no reinforcement tricks
{player} i'm done watching you win on the same flank. {village} is open. come and prove the mix
{player} i have a fight set at {town}. bring the same comp you used last time so we can compare the ratios

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and i took {troop_count} men through {enemy_faction}'s line clean. your timing was good. don't let it go to your head
{player} that was a clean split. your flank held and my reserves came in on time. note the spacing for next time
{player} your half of the line held when it should have broken. the ratio worked. don't get comfortable, the left side was close
{troop_count} men against {enemy_faction} and the comp held. credit the math, not the luck

ambient_brag.text: {troop_count} men in the field and {gold} in the chest. the mix is tighter than anyone else's on this server
{fief} garrison is at {troop_count}. the ratio is right. nobody else is counting it this closely
{gold} in reserve and no waste in the comp. that's the whole trick. the rest of you are still doing it by feel
cleared {fief} with {troop_count} and not one unit out of position. spacing is the difference

{fief} is ours now. {enemy_faction} brought the wrong comp and it showed
taking {fief} from {enemy_faction} was a ratio problem for them. next one goes on the ledger
{my_faction} holds {fief} now. recheck your garrisons, {enemy_faction}

{player} started on {fief}. i'll recount the garrison before you get a ram in
{player} you're at {fief}. the garrison numbers are not what you think. i'm not panicking

ambient_chatter.text: the roads out of {town} are muddy again. half the caravans are late and everyone blames the weather
lag near {village} is bad tonight. anyone else losing units to rubber-banding or is it just me
weather's clear over {town}. good for a rerun. i've got three fights to check before bed
{village} market prices went up again. if you're buying troops now you're paying the tax
someone should map the fords between {town} and {village}. cav routes matter more than people think

war_declared.text: The council has voted: {my_faction} will meet {enemy_faction} with steel. I did warn that patience was a virtue.
Blood is spilt on the council's word, and I shall make certain the minutes record who argued for it. Quietly, of course.
Every war is a lesson for those who did not vote. Let us hope the lessons are learned before the banners are.

peace_made.text: {my_faction} and {faction} have agreed terms at last. Peace is a fine thing, though some only discover it after losing.
The treaty with {faction} is signed, and I have already drafted the council's note of thanks. Credit is a matter of record.
{my_faction} is at peace with {faction}. Let it not be said the council cannot bend when bending serves it.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}! I always say the council is only as strong as the friends it keeps. Do sit near me.
Ser {player}, your oath to {my_faction} is noted. I shall arrange a seat for you at the next council, if you are willing.
{player} has joined {my_faction} at last. How refreshing to see someone arrive on time for once. Do try not to cause a stir.
I am delighted you chose {my_faction}, {player}. Loyalty of your sort is rarely forgotten in this hall.
{player} now swears to {my_faction}. Lovely. Now we shall see who keeps their word when the votes are close.

player_left_my_faction.text: How curious that {player} found {faction} so much more appealing than {my_faction}. I am sure they had their reasons.
Ser {player}, I shall not blame you for seeking better company. I shall, however, remember the oath you swore to {my_faction}.
{player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. A lesson for the council, I suppose: oaths are only as good as the purse behind them.
Departures from {my_faction} are never a surprise to me. I simply keep a list, and {player} has moved up it.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has been granted to {player}, and the council is pleased with the arrangement. I have no doubt it was a sound decision.
Ser {player}, I see {fief} now answers to you. Do govern it well. Your predecessors' records were never quite so tidy.
{player} was given {fief}. How generous the council is with its favours. I do hope the walls hold better than the promises did.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. I argued for you quietly in the hall, though I suspect you already know that.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: Ser {player}, {rival} has been courting {enemy_faction} behind the council's back. Shall we see that the hall hears of it?
{player}, a word in confidence. {enemy_faction} is ripe for a bargain, and {rival} is standing in the way. Interested?
Between us, {player}, I would sooner stand with you than with {rival}. Join me against {enemy_faction} and we both profit.
A small offer, {player}. Ally with me against {enemy_faction} and I will remember who helped when the votes fall.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} has fallen to {my_faction} at last, taken from {enemy_faction} in a fine piece of planning. The council will hear all about it.
The flag of {my_faction} now flies over {fief}. {enemy_faction} will be discussing that loss for some time, I imagine.
{fief} is ours. Credit goes to the council's wise votes, and I shall see that it does not forget who drafted them.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief}. Brave of them, though I wonder how long a fief stays grateful to a lord who gained it so quickly.
Ser {player}, you took {fief} from my hand. I shall not forget it, nor will the council, I promise you that.
{fief} has changed hands to {player}. A lesson for us all in how quickly a council's promises can be outpaced.
Ser {player}, well played with {fief}. Do enjoy it while the council is still deciding who really holds the deeds.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Good, {player}. Against {enemy_faction} we are stronger together, and {rival} can watch from the sidelines and wonder why.
Very well, {player}. I accept. Let us see if {rival} is still so confident when {enemy_faction} discovers our arrangement.
I accept gladly, {player}. Speak of this to no one yet. The walls of this hall have ears, and so do certain lords.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have no wish to be seen beside you while {rival} is still counting favours. Perhaps another season.
I must decline, {player}. Alliances are serious business, and I have a council to satisfy before I bind myself to anyone.
Not today, {player}, and I am sorry for it. {rival} has my ear at present, and a promise to them I cannot easily break.

ambient_chatter.text: Has anyone else noticed the mud around {town} this week? A council meeting in that weather is a test of patience. :)
The road from {village} was clear this morning, which I took as a sign. Good weather makes for better votes, I find.
Merchants in {town} are grumbling about tolls again. Someone ought to put it before the council, and I should be glad to.
Lag again on the eastern road, I see. Still, a quiet server gives a man time to think about who sits where at the next council.

encounter_greeting.text: Halt, ser {player}! I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I will not yield this road to any who would bar it. Stand aside or prove your mettle.
Good day, ser {player}. I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction}. Our paths cross upon this road, so let us part with honour and without bloodshed, traveller.
Well met, friend {player}! {persona} of {my_faction} greets you. My ancestors would weep to see two honest parties pass without a word of cheer.

encounter_threatened.text: Pay {gold} to a man who has sworn an oath? Keep your coin, ser {player}. You shall have steel before you have a single piece of silver from me.
You name a price of {gold} and a surrender in one breath, ser {player}. I have kept my oath through worse threats than yours. Speak plainer, or step back.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for you would not cheapen yourself with a demand of {gold}. Let us speak again when the blood has cooled.
{gold} for my surrender? The Ouzmar hammer has been broken before and I still stand. Come and take what you want, ser {player}, and let the saga record your shame.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept your proposal, ser {player}. Our banners shall stand together against {enemy_faction}, and my hammer will answer for the oath we swear.
By my oath, ser {player}, I accept! We shall break {enemy_faction} together, and the saga will name us allies in arms for generations.
Agreed, ser {player}. I will not share a fire with {rival}, but you I trust. Let us march against {enemy_faction} and let our word be the bond between us.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I must decline, ser {player}. An alliance is an oath, and I do not swear lightly. Perhaps when the moon is kinder we may speak of it again.
No, ser {player}. I will not bind my hammer to yours while you keep company with {rival}. Prove your honour first, and then we shall talk.
I regret I must refuse, ser {player}. Your offer is honourable, but my vow forbids it for now. Know that I remember your courtesy all the same.

captured_by_player.text: Bound and beaten, yet not broken, ser {player}. Ask your ransom of {my_faction} if you must, but know that I will not beg before you.
I am your captive, ser {player}, and I will not dispute it. {gold} is what you ask, and {my_faction} will pay it in time, for our oaths bind us to one another.
A fine stroke brought me low, ser {player}. You have my respect, and I shall tell my kin that you fought as an honest knight and held your captive with fairness.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you could have ransomed me and did not. I shall not forget this mercy, and my hammer owes you a debt.
Let it be known that ser {player} released me without ransom. Mercy such as that is rare on these roads, and my hammer honours it.
You loosed my chains, ser {player}, and asked nothing of me. I cannot yet call us friends, but I will not forget the mercy shown.
Ser {player} let me go rather than take my coin. I still count you a rival to my faction, but I will not deny the mercy you showed.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction} like a coward turning from the field. Let the saga record this betrayal.
Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Oaths are hard to keep and easy to break, so I shall judge by what you do next.
I grieve to see you leave {my_faction}, ser {player}, though I will not curse you. Your honour is still yours to keep, wherever you march.

war_declared.text: Upon my hammer's oath, {my_faction} takes up arms against {enemy_faction}! Let the saga remember which banners marched first.
Let the bells of {my_faction} ring out! War is declared on {enemy_faction}, and I shall stand in the first rank as my ancestors did.
{enemy_faction} has thrown down the gauntlet to {my_faction}. Very well, I accept it, and I shall answer with my hammer and my name.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, your shield stood beside mine at the ford. With {troop_count} blades we broke {enemy_faction}. I shall not forget it, friend.
Ser {player}, we fought as one with {troop_count} blades against {enemy_faction}, and not a man turned from the line. Such courage honours us both, traveller.

encounter_farewell.text: We part for now, ser {player}, but I shall not forget your face. When next we meet, let the hammer speak for us both.
Go well on your road, ser {player}. May your oaths be kept and your banners held high until we meet again.
Farewell, friend {player}. Walk in honour, and I shall walk in honour too. Until the roads cross again, my hand is open to you.
Begone for now, ser {player}. Our quarrel is not finished, and the saga shall not close until it is settled between us.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} is a fine omen for the smithies. A good hammer rings truest on a wet morning, friends.
Word from {village} is that the bread is thin this season. Still, the folk there keep their oaths, and I honour them for it.
Stalwart folk of {town}, keep your oaths and your forges burning. The saga is long and the road is longer still.
Someone in {village} called the road a grind. A grind? Speak of honest labour, not of such words, I beg you.
Tools sent to {town} under oath must be carried with care, for no lazy hand should touch a vow made in iron.
